Title: Open-channel admissions will not affect public university quotas, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Higher Education Ministry has assured that admissions to public universities through the open channel will not affect quotas allocated through the centralised UPU system.
Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said open-channel admissions accounted for only a small percentage of intake and were limited to courses with available places, rather than being driven solely by revenue considerations.
"I would like to inform this House that this issue does not arise at all, as we will maintain the quotas that have been set," he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
On tuition fee differences, Zambry acknowledged that they existed, particularly for critical courses.
He said the government continued to increase allocations and quotas for fields such as accounting, engineering and artificial intelligence to accommodate the high number of qualified students.
He said that poverty or financial constraints should not prevent students from accepting offers to study at public universities, as various forms of financial assistance were available.
"The government provides various forms of financial support covering tuition fees and living allowances, including the Community College Student Financial Assistance, Foundation Financial Assistance and B40 TVET Scholarships," he added.
Meanwhile, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said Malaysia recorded 32.26 million international visitor arrivals from January to September this year, a 2.4 per cent increase from the same period last year.
He said the government continued to intensify tourism promotion using existing allocations to sustain growth, particularly amid global geopolitical challenges affecting travel plans.
To improve international connectivity, Tiong said Tourism Malaysia had partnered 24 airlines – three domestic and 21 international – to support 46 international routes from January to October this year.
"Of these, 35 were new routes while the remaining 11 were existing routes that continued to operate. They included Xi'an-Kuala Lumpur, Guiyang-Kuala Lumpur, Shanghai-Tawau, Xiamen-Kota Kinabalu, Busan-Kuala Lumpur and Frankfurt-Kuala Lumpur, as well as charter flights from Warsaw, Poland, and Almaty, Kazakhstan, scheduled for December," he said.
The business events segment, including meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE), also performed well, with its economic impact rising 113.7 per cent to RM1.24 billion in the second quarter of this year.
The number of events increased 81.2 per cent to 125, while international delegate attendance rose 105.2 per cent to 83,596.
Tiong said RM10 million had been allocated to the Malaysia Convention and Exhibition Bureau (MyCEB) to attract more high-impact MICE and international sporting events. Tax incentives for organising international-standard events had also been extended for 2028 to 2030.
Meanwhile, Deputy Dewan Rakyat Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Ramli Mohd Nor thanked the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry for its cooperation in organising the Sewang Festival, which brought together 18 Orang Asli ethnic groups on Oct 24.
He said the festival had the potential to attract international tourists, with a national-level edition targeted for next year.

Title: Tiger sightings spark fear among 500 Kuala Krai villagers
Article:
KUALA KRAI: About 500 residents in four villages in Mukim Sungai Mengkuang are living in fear after a tiger was spotted near a forest in the area more than two weeks ago.
Their concerns intensified after a cow belonging to a villager was believed to have been attacked by the tiger on Monday. Footprints believed to belong to a tigress and her cub were also found.
The affected villages are Kampung Nara, Kampung Bukit Pacat, Kampung Gajah Mati and Kampung Slow Temiang.
Resident Mansor Derahman, 77, said he had stopped tapping rubber for more than two weeks for fear of encountering the animal, especially after hearing its roars near his rubber plantation.
"For now, I have decided not to go to the plantation because I am worried about running into the tiger. We do not know when or where it might appear.
"Most residents here depend on rubber tapping as their main source of income. However, since the animal appeared, many have been afraid to risk their safety by going to their plantations," he said.
Another rubber tapper, Sukarman Ibrahim, 59, said he found fresh tiger footprints along the path to his plantation about two weeks ago.
He said he was on his way to tap rubber at 8am when he spotted the footprints on wet ground following light rain the previous night.
"Based on their sizes, I noticed two sets of footprints, one large and the other smaller. I believe they belonged to an adult tiger and its cub.
"I immediately turned back because I was worried about my safety. I also heard the animal roaring from a nearby hill," he said.
Meanwhile, Sungai Mengkuang village head Zulkifli Sulaiman said this was the first tiger sighting reported to him in his 17 years in the position.
Previously, he had received reports of wild animals such as elephants, bears and tapirs in the area.
He said residents were taking precautions by avoiding outdoor activities after Maghrib. Those needing to go out in an emergency would only do so in vehicles such as cars or pick-up trucks.
The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) has also installed two traps, one each in Kampung Nara and Kampung Gajah Mati, more than a week ago in an effort to capture the tiger.
Zulkifli said the presence of the tiger and its cub had affected residents' livelihoods, as many were afraid to resume rubber tapping for fear of being attacked.

Title: Zahari backs BN's Durian Tunggal candidate despite being dropped
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Not being selected to contest in the Melaka election has not deterred former Durian Tunggal assemblyman Datuk Zahari Khalil from serving the community, as he continues to campaign alongside his friend and Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa.
Zahari said he was not disappointed with the party's decision to field another candidate, and remained committed to Umno and BN and the people of Durian Tunggal.
He said he had continued meeting residents since the candidates were announced and would support Mustafa, better known as Cikgu Mus, if he won the seat.
"My struggle in Umno and BN must continue. I entered politics not for rank or position, but to serve the people in my village and help the Durian Tunggal community.
"I am not disappointed because the person replacing me is my own friend, Cikgu Mus. Why should I be disappointed?" he said while meeting residents with Mustafa at Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, today.
Zahari, a former state deputy works, infrastructure, public amenities and transport executive councillor, said his five years as an elected representative had taught him to appreciate both the party that nominated him and the residents who had supported him.
He said he was also touched by the support he had received from the residents, including those he barely knew, following the decision not to renominate him.
On banners that went viral at several locations calling for him to continue leading Durian Tunggal, Zahari said the support had encouraged him to keep serving the community despite not contesting this time.
He urged voters to continue supporting BN and Mustafa to ensure development and services in the constituency continued.
"I will not be going anywhere. I will continue working with Cikgu Mus, including if he wins this election.
"I will also ask him to continue the work I have done for the sake of the people of Durian Tunggal," he said.
Mustafa said he appreciated Zahari's support, describing him as a long-time friend and fellow party member, and expressed confidence that their cooperation would help sustain development efforts in Durian Tunggal.
He said they had known each other since their days in the Umno Youth movement and had worked together for years in the Alor Gajah parliamentary constituency.
"As party members and political fighters, we must respect the party's decisions.
"I have known Datuk Zahari for a long time. We are good friends and have fought alongside each other since our Youth days.
"With his guidance, advice and support, I am confident we can continue his work as a team," he said before leaving to collect his appointment letter in Kuala Lumpur.
Mustafa added that he was familiar with parts of Durian Tunggal and its residents, and would build on the services provided by the previous elected representative.

Title: Bursa Malaysia opens higher on improved sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday as market sentiment improved, tracking overnight gains on Wall Street following fresh artificial intelligence (AI)-related funding announcements.
At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 3.39 points, or 0.21 per cent, to 1,615.24 from Tuesday's close of 1,611.85.
The benchmark index opened 2.64 points higher at 1,614.49.
Across the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 251 to 94, while 297 counters were unchanged, 2,225 untraded, and 104 suspended.
Turnover stood at 218.30 million units worth RM87.52 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said overnight Wall Street ended higher as investors turned their attention to upcoming corporate earnings reports, particularly those from the technology sector.
"Back home, the FBM KLCI closed higher yesterday above the 1,610 level on bargain hunting, supported mainly by local funds.
"Buying interest was evident in utility counters, which came under heavy selling pressure the previous day. For today, we expect the index to hover within the 1,605-1,615 range," he told Bernama.
Among the heavyweight stocks, Maybank rose one sen to RM10.00, while CIMB added two sen to RM7.13. Public Bank, Tenaga Nasional and IHH Healthcare were all flat at RM4.75, RM13.30 and RM7.84, respectively.
In active trade, Zetrix AI and MQ Technology inched up half a sen each to nine sen and six sen, respectively. VS Industry, MYMBN and Dagang Nexchange added one sen each to 35.5 sen, 17.5 sen and 45 sen, respectively.
Nestle led the top gainers, adding RM2.38 to RM96.66, while Malaysian Pacific Industries added 30 sen to RM41.60. Far East Holdings rose 25 sen to RM4.20, while MI Technovation and Hong Leong Bank went up 16 sen each to RM6.91 and RM21.36, respectively.
Among the top losers, United Plantations lost 38 sen to RM29.32, Westports Holdings declined 16 sen to RM6.92, Farm Fresh decreased seven sen to RM1.81, SAM Engineering & Equipment slid six sen to RM4.25 and Hengyuan Refining Company shed five sen to RM4.06.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index increased 23.53 points to 12,062.82, the FBM Top 100 Index rose 21.02 points to 11,855.55, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 14.68 points to 17,384.80, the FBM Emas Shariah Index was 20.98 points higher at 12,070.71 and the FBM ACE Index went up 27.12 points to 5,445.75.
Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.30 of a point to 177.21, the Energy Index increased 6.30 points to 852.04, the Financial Services Index jumped 31.79 points to 18,632.82 and the Plantation Index improved 6.32 points to 8,660.58.

Title: Kee Ming earnings set to jump on data centre, solar projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kee Ming Group Bhd is expected to post stronger earnings of RM7 million to RM9 million in the second quarter of the financial year 2027 (Q2 FY27), up 16 to 40 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ).
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd (Maybank IB) said the earnings growth would be driven by progress in its data centre electrical fit-out and solar interconnection facility (IF) projects.
The projected earnings of RM7 million to RM9 million would be higher than the RM6.4 million recorded in Q1 FY27.
The firm maintained its "Buy" call on the stock and raised its sum-of-the-parts-based target price to RM3.10 from RM2.42, based on an unchanged 20 times FY28 estimated price-to-earnings ratio.
It also raised its earnings forecasts on Kee Ming for FY27 to FY29 by 9.0 per cent to 22 per cent, reflecting improved profit margin assumptions and stronger prospects for new contract replenishment.
"Our margin assumption remains conservative versus Q1 FY27's, factoring in potential headcount cost increases as Kee Ming expands to support its growing project pipeline," it said.
Maybank IB said the company's tender book had grown 27 per cent QoQ to RM2.8 billion, supported by opportunities across industrial projects, data centres and high-voltage power infrastructure, including Tenaga Nasional Bhd-related and solar IF projects.
The firm anticipates solar IF projects linked to the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme to ramp up, with tenders expected to be called in the fourth quarter of calendar year 2027.
Maybank IB said this is expected to support higher contract replenishment in FY28 and FY29, backed by Kee Ming's synergies with Solarvest Bhd, which has historically secured about 30 per cent of the market share in utility-scale solar projects.
"We take this opportunity to raise our replenishment forecast from RM350 million to RM470 million across FY2-FY29, reflecting its stronger ongoing and future tender pipeline," it added.

Title: Nestle Malaysia rides demand recovery, secures higher earnings forecasts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd is expected to sustain earnings growth in the fourth quarter of 2026, supported by resilient demand and improving cost efficiencies, says CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
Analyst Walter Aw Lik Hsin said improving cost efficiencies and operating leverage should help cushion higher input costs, although earnings could moderate quarter-on-quarter due to a higher cost base.
He said government cash assistance under the 2027 Budget, particularly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah, should support household purchasing power and demand for Nestle Malaysia's products.
"We also expect the continuation of cash assistance and higher minimum wages to lift disposable income, particularly among lower- to middle-income households, providing a favourable demand backdrop for Nestle Malaysia's products into financial year 2027 (FY27)," he said in a note.
Aw said the company's third-quarter performance reflected improving domestic demand as boycott-related pressures eased, contributions from new product launches and resilient export sales, particularly Malaysia-made halal products.
Revenue rose 5.3 per cent year-on-year to RM1.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026, while core net profit increased 64.7 per cent to RM206 million after adjusting for one-off items, mainly a RM7.9 million net foreign exchange loss.
For the first nine months of 2026, revenue grew 6.7 per cent year-on-year, while core net profit rose 32.4 per cent to RM555 million, outpacing sales growth on improved margins and operating leverage.
Nestle Malaysia declared an interim dividend of 80 sen a share, bringing its total dividend per share for the nine-month period to RM1.60, equivalent to a 67 per cent payout ratio.
Aw said margin resilience should continue despite higher commodity prices in the second half of 2026, as prices of key inputs such as cocoa, coffee and sugar remained below their 2025 peaks.
"We expect near-term cost pressure to be manageable, mitigated by better cost control, economies of scale, inventory buffers from forward purchases, and Nestle's global sourcing network.
"These should help cushion input cost volatility amid ongoing geopolitical tensions and El Nino–related supply risks into the first half of 2027," he said.
The company is also expected to optimise its sales mix through new product launches and a greater focus on higher-margin categories, while stronger domestic volumes should support operating leverage.
Although selective price increases remain an option to offset higher costs, Aw said Nestle Malaysia was likely to prioritise affordability.
CIMB Securities nevertheless expects gross profit margin to moderate to 32.5 per cent in 2027 and 32.6 per cent in 2028, from 33.1 per cent in 2026, reflecting a higher average input cost environment.
Following the stronger-than-expected nine-month results, the firm raised the company's earnings per share forecasts for 2026 to 2028 by between 8.1 per cent and 17.2 per cent.
CIMB Securities kept its "Buy" call with a higher target price of RM118 from RM115, citing Nestle Malaysia's established brand portfolio, defensive earnings profile and exposure to essential consumption.
Hong Leong Investment Bank also kept its "Buy" call on the stock but lowered the target price to RM121 from RM135, based on the dividend discount model (DDM), with a weighted average cost of capital of 6.8 per cent and terminal growth rate of 3.5 per cent
Its analyst Jonathan Ooi said the revision reflects an increase in the risk-free rate to 4.0 per cent from 3.0 per cent, in line with the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yield, which more than offsets the earnings upgrade.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing 14-year-old boy attacked by crocodile found dead
Article:
SEBUYAU: A 14-year-old boy who was reported missing after being attacked by a crocodile in Ulu Sungai Plaie was found dead about 800m from the Kampung Tuba jetty at 8pm yesterday.
The victim, Mohd Nordin Mohd Othman, was found with several body parts missing.
A Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department operations centre spokesman said the discovery followed a report from a Kampung Tuba villager who spotted a crocodile carrying something in its mouth about 6pm.
The villager was returning home after visiting the victim's family in Kampung Plaie when he saw the crocodile.
"The resident returned to the location about 8pm and found the victim's body, which was believed to have been regurgitated by the crocodile," the spokesman said.
The victim was identified by his grandfather, Dana Randi.
Initial examination found that several body parts were missing, with bite marks and other injuries on the body.
Police later took the remains to Simunjan Hospital for further action.
The boy was reportedly attacked by a crocodile while loading oil palm fruit into a boat at Sungai Plaie, Ulu Sebuyau, on Monday.
The incident, which occurred at 5.30pm, was witnessed by his uncle, Midin Radin, who then informed the Sungai Plaie village head.
Following the discovery, the search and rescue operation was called off at 4am today.

Title: 3 arrested after Alza drives against traffic to evade police in Johor
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Three men were arrested and another is being sought after they allegedly drove against traffic on the Second Link Expressway to evade a police check.
Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said the three suspects comprised a Malaysian and two Filipinos.
He said the incident occurred about 2.30am when a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit was conducting crime prevention patrols along Jalan Persiaran SILC in Gelang Patah.
Police spotted a Perodua Alza carrying four men behaving suspiciously and ordered the driver to stop for a check.
The driver sped off and entered the Second Link Expressway against traffic.
He later abandoned the car at Jalan Suria 2 in Masai and fled on foot. Police arrested three suspects, while the fourth remains at large, Radin Ramlan said.
A search of the car found a cable cutter, which police seized along with the vehicle and three mobile phones.
Urine tests found that two suspects were positive for methamphetamine.
Investigations are ongoing to locate the remaining suspect and determine whether the men were involved in other criminal activities. Preliminary findings suggest they intended to steal cables, Radin Ramlan said in a statement yesterday.
A three-minute video showing the car fleeing the police check, believed to have been recorded by a customer at a nearby restaurant, went viral on social media.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver killed after car hits wild boar, crashes into lorry
Article:
HULU SELANGOR: A driver was killed after his car hit a wild boar, swerved and crashed into a lorry near a petrol station in Kalumpang.
The 7.16am incident involved a 53-year-old man.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said a team from the Kuala Kubu Baru Fire and Rescue Station was deployed to the scene.
Firefighters initially found the driver trapped in the vehicle and unconscious.
The driver was later confirmed dead by the Health Ministry.
Photographs shared by the fire department showed the front of the car was badly damaged.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man to face charges over ramming GOF vehicle during police pursuit
Article:
PASIR MAS: A 35-year-old man is expected to face three charges at the Pasir Mas magistrate's court today after ramming a General Operations Force (GOF) vehicle during a police pursuit.
The suspect, dressed in lock-up attire, arrived at the court in a police truck at 8.50am.
He is expected to be charged under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and Section 186 of the Penal Code.
The charges relate to dangerous driving, a drug-related offence and obstructing a public servant in the discharge of his duties, respectively.
On Oct 24, the suspect allegedly
rammed a four-wheel-drive vehicle
carrying four GOF personnel during a pursuit along Jalan Pekan Lama, Rantau Panjang.
The collision left a 41-year-old corporal with a fractured right arm, while the three other personnel escaped unhurt.
The suspect was arrested after the Toyota Camry he was driving became immobilised.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2,097 police personnel arrested for drugs, robbery, corruption since 2021
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 2,097 police personnel and officers were arrested for drug, robbery and corruption offences from 2021 to August this year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said of these, 1,551 were arrested for drug offences, 64 for robbery and 482 by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
In a written parliamentary reply to Lim Lip Eng (PH-Kepong), who asked for the number of police personnel arrested for the offences since 2021, Saifuddin provided a yearly breakdown.
Of the drug-related arrests under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, 357 were recorded in 2021, 248 in 2022, 245 in 2023, 310 in 2024, 256 in 2025 and 135 from January to August this year.
Robbery arrests totalled 64, comprising 10 each in 2021 and 2022, 11 in 2023, 13 in 2024, 10 in 2025 and 10 in the first eight months of this year.
The MACC arrested 482 police personnel over the same period: 77 in 2021, 86 in 2022, 129 in 2023, 53 in 2024, 87 in 2025 and 50 from January to August this year.
Lim also sought an
update
on the investigation into 12 policemen suspected of robbing a group of foreigners of about RM200,000 in cryptocurrency at Country Heights, Kajang, in February.
Saifuddin said police had opened an investigation paper into the Feb 5 incident and were investigating it under Section 395 of the Penal Code.
The 12 policemen, including four from Bukit Aman's Commercial Crime Investigation Department, were arrested after a Chinese national lodged a report over a raid on a rented bungalow in Country Heights on Feb 5.
Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the policemen had been assigned desk duties to ensure the investigation could proceed properly.
The victims' lawyer had questioned the
lack of updates
on the investigation and said he would write to the investigating officer and the Attorney-General's Chambers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMEA to probe fatal boat collision off Perlis
Article:
KUALA NERANG: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) will conduct an internal investigation into a boat collision that killed its sailor off Perlis on Monday night.
MMEA deputy director-general (Operations) Maritime Vice-Admiral Mohd Zawawi Abdullah said the investigation would identify shortcomings and determine whether standard operating procedures (SOPs) needed to be improved to prevent similar incidents.
He said the agency had specific SOPs for every operation and regularly reminded personnel to comply with them.
"Whenever an incident occurs, a post-mortem or internal investigation is conducted to identify shortcomings that can be addressed through improvements," he told reporters after the funeral of Senior Maritime Petty Officer (Technical) Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, at the Muslim cemetery of Masjid Tengku Sarafudin Badlishah here last night.
Zawawi said the investigation would also examine the training and operational equipment.
"Internal investigations are usually initiated as soon as possible and may take a few weeks to complete.
"We want to determine whether any SOPs need to be refined for the benefit of all MMEA personnel and to prevent similar incidents from recurring," he said.
[[nid:1565128]]
He said the incident would not dampen personnel morale but would strengthen their resolve to safeguard the nation's maritime security.
On the welfare of Roshaimi's family, Zawawi said the agency would ensure his widow and two school-going children received appropriate assistance in accordance with existing procedures.
Roshaimi was killed and three others injured when
their boat
reportedly struck a concrete structure off Kuala Sungai Padang, near Kuala Perlis, about 11pm on Monday.
The team were pursuing a boat suspected of carrying undocumented migrants when the collision occurred.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GOF arrests 55 suspected human smugglers in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) has arrested 55 suspected
tekong darat
(human smugglers), including six women, allegedly behind migrant smuggling along the Kelantan border since last year.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said 35 were arrested last year and another 20 this year.
Radzi said those arrested comprised 49 men and six women, including citizens of Thailand, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Pakistan.
He said the GOF was targeting not only undocumented migrants entering the country illegally but also the smugglers and networks managing their entry.
"This is important to ensure smuggling activities are disrupted at the network level," he said when contacted.
Radzi said integrated operations along the border would be intensified to curb human smuggling, as syndicates were becoming increasingly brazen and had allegedly threatened villagers.
Asked about claims that syndicates had threatened residents with firearms, Radzi said they were becoming more cunning and willing to take risks, particularly as enforcement along smuggling routes was tightened and many illegal jetties had been closed.
He said the GOF took seriously recent claims by residents along the Kelantan coast that they had been threatened with a pistol after encountering individuals believed to be linked to human smuggling.
However, the allegations had yet to be verified, as the police had not received an official report from the residents.
"We do not want to confirm the use or possession of firearms by syndicates without valid evidence. Any allegations will be
examined and investigated
based on the information and evidence obtained," he said.
Radzi also reminded GOF personnel to prioritise safety, act in accordance with the law and remain alert to threats.
Yesterday, media reports quoted residents along the Kelantan coast as claiming they had been threatened with firearms by individuals believed to be involved in human smuggling syndicates to prevent them from exposing the illegal activities.
The allegations have raised concern among local communities, amid claims that undocumented migrants were brought ashore almost every night through rivers, jetties and secluded coastal areas.
A local resident identified only as Hamidi, 42, was reported as saying the activities occurred frequently, with individuals suspected of involvement in smuggling and those believed to be acting as lookouts, or "tonto", allegedly operating in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah fire dept: 'Bomba' vehicle in viral video is not ours
Article:
ALOR STAR: The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department has confirmed that a private vehicle bearing the word "Bomba" and fitted with a beacon light does not belong to the department or any Volunteer Fire Brigade in the state.
In a statement today, the department said it was aware of a video circulating on social media showing the vehicle and was taking further action over the unauthorised use of its identity.
"We take a serious view of any unauthorised use of the department's identity, which could mislead the public and undermine the image and credibility of the fire service," it said.
The department also thanked members of the public who had provided information, adding that their cooperation was essential to ensuring the accuracy of information in circulation.
"We remain committed to upholding the integrity and professionalism of the department while maintaining public trust in the fire service," it added.
A five-second video recently went viral on social media, showing a private vehicle bearing the word "Bomba" and fitted with a warning light allegedly nearly colliding with several vehicles after running a red light in Sungai Petani.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US costs of Iran war rise to over US$47bil
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US military has spent more than US$47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran, more than 25 per cent higher than the Defence Department's estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters.
The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its estimate, which has not been shared publicly.
The disclosure about the rising cost of the Iran war comes as Republicans wrestle with the political fallout of the unpopular conflict ahead of the Nov 3 election that will determine control of Congress for the next two years.
The war's impact on global energy costs has weighed on support for Republican candidates and hurt President Donald Trump's approval ratings. Trump's Republican Party holds a narrow majority in both chambers of Congress.
The Pentagon's latest estimate was tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than US$29 billion to replace expended munitions used in the conflict.
More than US$6 billion would be needed to replace military equipment and so-called "platform losses", which include the loss of aircraft, including many drones lost during the war.
Trump launched the Iran war jointly with Israel in February, predicting that the conflict would last a short time.
Trump's initial strategy in the Iran war focused on first using expensive, high-end precision missiles to bomb Iran's defences so it could later use less expensive munitions, including gravity bombs like the air-launched JDAMs, which are plentiful.
But an April ceasefire gave time for Iran to dig out underground storage facilities, bringing back online some Iranian defences, as well as missiles and drones that had been inaccessible.
Trump has since imposed a naval blockade on Iran to starve it of oil export revenue and held out the possibility of restarting combat operations after the midterm elections. US officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, say the Pentagon has been planning to restart heavy fighting if ordered to do so.
The latest Pentagon estimate compares with Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's July estimate of US$37.5 billion for the cost of the war.
While the figures include a host of operational costs, from flight operations to cyber support, the US military's Iran war cost estimates did not clearly account for the massive expense expected to repair damage to US bases sustained by Iranian missile and drone attacks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US new home sales cooled in September as mortgage rates surged
Article:
WASHINGTON: The sale of new US homes slowed in September, government data showed Tuesday, as surging mortgage rates weighed on homebuyers and affordability worries bite.
New home sales were down by 0.6 per cent from August, reaching a seasonally-adjusted annual rate of 676,000 last month, said the Commerce Department.
While the figure beat expectations of 653,000 according to a forecast published by MarketWatch, it was still 5.3 per cent below the rate seen the same month a year ago.
The cooldown comes as US mortgage rates exceeded 7.0 per cent last month, reaching their highest level since President Donald Trump returned to the White House.
The popular 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 7.03 per cent in late September, Freddie Mac data showed, underscoring voters' affordability concerns as US midterm elections approach next month.
Cost of living worries and climbing mortgage rates have been bogging down property sales this year, with American households facing increased pressure from soaring gasoline costs.
The median sales price of new homes sold in September rose 3.9 per cent month-on-month to US$400,400.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australia's central bank set to weigh if rate hikes are enough to curb inflation
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia's central bank will debate whether four rate hikes this year will prove sufficient to return inflation to target at next week's policy meeting, the bank's governor said on Wednesday.
Michele Bullock, the governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia told lawmakers oil and related prices had increased sharply again and would add materially to inflation.
"A key question is whether the tightening in monetary policy to date will be sufficient to bring inflation back to target in a reasonable time," Bullock added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump floats idea of Venezuela becoming '51st state'
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday suggested that Venezuela could become the 51st US state, citing growing oil cooperation between the two countries, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
"I want to thank Venezuela, where our relationship has become very, very good, a great one," Trump told supporters at a midterm election rally in Corpus Christi, Texas.
Trump announced the arrival of the first one million barrels of free Venezuelan oil under an agreement between the two countries.
"This historic win gives us control over a massive part of the world's oil supply," he said.
"It will be refined here in Texas – including right here in Corpus Christi," he added.
Trump said investments were creating jobs in Venezuela on a scale he claimed would have been unimaginable a year earlier.
"We're bringing out a lot of oil for ourselves, a lot. It will become a prosperous country, and who knows? Maybe someday soon it will become a prosperous 51st state. That's possible," he said.
The US president then repeated the suggestion, proposing that Venezuela could have a governor instead of a president.
"Let's make it. Let's make it the 51st state. And instead of a president, we'll have an election for a governor. How about that? You know, they have a lot of oil," Trump said.

Title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar for eight consecutive trading days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar for the eighth consecutive trading day today, reflecting continued positive momentum in the local currency at the start of trading.
At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0855/0915 against the US dollar from Tuesday's close of 4.0865/0900.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said optimism in the financial market, driven by the artificial intelligence (AI)-related theme, continued to dominate global equities, providing support for the Malaysian currency.
Meanwhile, he said the US Federal Reserve (Fed) is expected to keep the federal funds rate steady between 3.75 per cent and 4.0 per cent.
"On that note, the ringgit is likely to continue trading within a narrow range as traders weigh external developments to determine their trading direction.
The ringgit is expected to hover between RM4.07 and RM4.08 against the US dollar today," he told Bernama.
The local note also traded higher against a basket of major currencies.
The ringgit strengthened against the British pound to 5.4362/4441 from 5.4412/4458 at Tuesday's close, advanced vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5858/5897 from 2.5903/5927 and climbed against the euro to 4.5459/5526 from 4.5524/5563.
Meanwhile, the ringgit traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It traded slightly higher against the Singapore dollar to 3.1881/1932 from 3.1883/1913 at Tuesday's close, and edged up against the Thai baht to 12.0884/1115 from 12.1010/1160 previously.
The local note was almost flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 225.0/225.4 from 225.0/225.3 and the Philippine peso at 6.36/6.38 from 6.36/6.37.

Title: Air quality stays healthy nationwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality remains at healthy levels nationwide, with no areas recording unhealthy readings.
A total of 43 monitoring stations recorded moderate Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7.50am.
The Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System showed that nine states and two Federal Territories recorded moderate readings.
They were Johor, Sarawak, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Sabah, Melaka, Selangor, Perak, Penang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Another 25 monitoring stations recorded good air quality.
API readings of zero to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected in Langkawi, Kedah, and Pulau Tioman, Pahang, until 9am.
Similar weather conditions were expected in Sarawak, affecting Kuching and Samarahan, including Asajaya and Sebuyau.

Title: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
Article:
NEW YORK: An AI-fuelled tech rally sent US stocks to a higher close on Tuesday as third-quarter reporting season gained steam, while the Federal Reserve convened for its penultimate meeting of the year.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq led the gains.
The buzz surrounding details of Anthropic's impending initial public offering helped boost chip stocks for the third consecutive session.
Growing concerns over the viability of debt-funded spending amid rising borrowing costs have weighed on the AI trade this month. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index, while off more than 20 per cent from its June 22 record closing high, has outperformed the broader market this year, gaining 62.1 per cent compared with the S&P 500's 12.8 per cent year-to-date advance.
To fund its AI expansion, Meta increased its largest-ever equity fundraising to US$97.5 billion, sending the Facebook parent's shares down 1.6 per cent.
"(The Anthropic news) seems to be giving a little bit of a relief rally to the AI stocks, particularly the semis," said Chuck Carlson, CEO at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana, referring to chip stocks. "Those stocks have gotten clobbered in recent weeks and they were probably due for a bounce."
Economic data showed rising new orders for computers and peripheral equipment, supporting the notion of strong AI-related spending.
Nearly half of S&P 500 companies have reported third-quarter results. Of those, 83 per cent have delivered better-than-expected results, according to the most recent available LSEG data.
Boeing tumbled 10.7 per cent following its bigger-than-expected third-quarter loss, while water-management company Xylem slid 14.2 per cent after trimming full-year forecasts.
United Parcel Service advanced 5.8 per cent after the package delivery firm raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts.
Sherwin-Williams' quarterly profit miss sent the stock 2.7 per cent lower, weighing on the Dow.
Royal Caribbean rose 5.5 per cent after the cruise operator lifted its full-year profit forecast.
Microsoft and Alphabet results are expected on Wednesday, while Amazon.com is due to report on Thursday.
The Fed convened on Tuesday for its October monetary policy meeting, which is widely expected to culminate in a decision to keep the fed funds target rate on hold in the 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent range, saving its second rate hike of the year for its final meeting in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
"There seems to be more confidence that the Fed isn't going to do anything at this meeting, partly because we have an election on Tuesday," Carlson added. "There's probably at least some relief that the rate situation is not going to get in the way of a rally."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 15.99 points, or 0.03 per cent, to 52,377.57, the S&P 500 gained 45.83 points, or 0.60 per cent, to 7,722.60 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 308.43 points, or 1.18 per cent, to 26,477.81.
Of the 11 major sectors in the S&P 500, technology led the gainers, while energy shares suffered the steepest percentage decline, hit by easing crude prices as attention turned to Middle East peace negotiations.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.83-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 81 new highs and 146 new lows on the NYSE.
On the Nasdaq, 3,118 stocks rose and 1,680 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.86-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 11 new 52-week highs and six new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 62 new highs and 239 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was 16.10 billion shares, compared with the 17.18 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

Title: Climate change must be declared 'global health emergency': Lancet study
Article:
PARIS: Climate change must be declared a "global health emergency" to shape governments' policies after heat caused three million deaths between 2016 and 2023, a report in The Lancet said Wednesday.
Published by the British medical journal ahead of the COP 31 climate summit in November, the 10th edition of the report brought together 146 researchers from 30 countries to assess the impact of climate change on the health of the world's population.
It said there were a record 710,000 heat-related deaths in 2023 with more than 70 per cent of that toll linked to human-caused climate change.
Marina Romanello, the executive director of the health and climate research project Lancet Countdown, said there were "three million heat-related deaths globally in an eight-year span since the Paris Agreement" of 2015.
"That's roughly equivalent to the entire population of Wales being wiped out in the space of eight years due to heat," she told a news conference.
And "68 per cent of those deaths are directly attributable to climate change."
The legally binding international climate treaty adopted in the French capital aimed to limit global warming to well below 2C and pursue efforts to keep it to 1.5C compared to pre-industrial levels.
- Climate change impact -
Romanello said the global health emergency due to climate change should have "an integrated approach so that we're not responding to emergency after emergency."
Instead she called for "a cohesive long-term response that builds resilience, builds capacities, and builds the possibilities of countries to avoid further emergencies moving forward."
To determine the share of deaths attributable to warming caused by human activity, the researchers compiled the number of heat-related deaths recorded by states, then subtracted those that would have occurred in the absence of climate change, said Professor Ollie Jay of the University of Sydney.
Jay said the intensity and frequency of periods of intense heat were amplified by climate change, pointing out that last year an extreme drought affected more than half of the world's land surface for at least one month.
- Economic cost -
By reducing worker productivity, warming has cost the global economy more than one trillion dollars per year over the past three years, the researchers said.
Southeast Asia and Africa, the hardest-hit regions, are estimated to have lost the equivalent of 3.9 per cent and 3.2 per cent of their GDP, compared with 0.2 per cent for Europe and 1.5 per cent for the Americas.
However there has been concrete progress in some areas.
Since 2016, 56 of the WHO's 194 member states have adapted their health and early-warning systems to anticipate extreme events.
Investment in clean energy reached $2.1 trillion in 2025 — double that of the amount invested in fossil fuels, which cause climate change.
However fossil fuels still account for 80 per cent of global energy, causing air pollution that results in 2.73 million deaths per year, the study said.
Meanwhile, roughly 323,000 deaths have been avoided in "at least" 77 countries where air pollution from fossil fuels has fallen since 2016, according to the report.
Although funding for climate-related medical research has increased sevenfold to reach $316 million in 2024, 84 per cent of these funds go to researchers in wealthy countries, even though the least developed nations are the most affected by the growing climate-related health threats.
Romanello said this year for the first time the researchers' work was complicated by the disappearance of certain data sources, particularly from the United States, such as fossil fuel subsidies, which have not been made public by the US authorities.
And for the past two years, global geopolitical instability has pushed global warming and its health impact into the background, she said, stressing that inaction was exacerbating the situation. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-cop seeks A-G's intervention over 2015 assault complaint against Shuhaily
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former policeman has sought the Attorney-General's intervention to revive an assault complaint lodged against Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain in 2015.
The move comes a week after Shuhaily was charged with two counts of voluntarily causing hurt to two police personnel at KLIA last month.
Lawyers Kamal Hisham Ja'afar and Muhammad Nor Tamrin said their client, Saifuddin Abdul Kader, lodged a police report against Shuhaily on Nov 19, 2015, when the latter was Hilir Perak police chief.
However, they claimed no action had been taken on the complaint.
"We received information from the public about a complainant who was allegedly assaulted by Shuhaily in 2015.
"Although a police report was lodged, no action has been taken against Shuhaily to date," they said in a statement today.
The lawyers said Saifuddin, then a junior police officer, had faced various career difficulties after lodging the report, eventually leading to his dismissal from the force.
According to the report, Saifuddin alleged that the incident occurred at 8.30am on Nov 17, 2015, while he was on guard duty at the Hilir Perak police headquarters.
He claimed Shuhaily reprimanded him for failing to salute him before repeatedly scolding him in front of other police personnel.
Saifuddin also alleged that Shuhaily punched his left wrist during the confrontation and threatened to transfer him to Sabah or Sarawak and initiate disciplinary action against him.
The lawyers said their client believed he now had an opportunity to seek justice following the A-G's decision to prosecute Shuhaily over the separate KLIA incident.
"Having seen the principle of equality before the law without discrimination demonstrated by the A-G in bringing charges against Shuhaily, Saifuddin believes he still has an opportunity to obtain justice under the current administration.
"We respectfully request that this case be reviewed and reconsidered to ensure that the rule of law continues to be upheld without discrimination," they said.
On Oct 21,
Shuhaily pleaded not guilty
at the Sepang Magistrate's Court to two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to two police personnel at KLIA on Sept 28.
Both charges were framed under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.

Title: 1MDB liabilities, BUDI95 among issues to be raised in Dewan Rakyat today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The status of efforts to settle 1Malaysia Development Bhd's (1MDB) remaining net liabilities, estimated at RM20.1 billion, including assets and claims still being recovered, is among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper published on Parliament's website, Lee Chuan How (PH-Ipoh Timor) will ask the Finance Minister for an update on the matter, including the amount expected to be recovered from each claim and the government's target year for fully settling the outstanding liabilities.
Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan (PN-Permatang Pauh) will also seek an explanation from the Finance Minister on the rationale behind the reduction in the Budi MADANI RON95 (BUDI95) subsidised petrol quota from 300 litres to 200 litres before it was increased again on September 1, 2026.
Other issues expected to be raised include data centre operations, plans to upgrade federal and state roads, and measures to address learning loss among pupils from hardcore poor households.
Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong) is scheduled to ask the Works Minister about plans to upgrade federal and state roads in Bentong to cope with increased traffic following the completion of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project.
Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal (PN-Machang) will seek details of the government's contingency plans to ensure that data centre operations do not compromise electricity and water supplies for the public during droughts or supply disruptions.
Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar (BN-Kinabatangan) will seek clarification on the government's strategic action plan to assist pupils from multidimensionally hardcore poor households who continue to experience long-term learning loss.
Following the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to resume the winding-up of the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 by the respective ministries.

Title: 1,600 Lembah Pantai families get RM150 Deepavali vouchers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: About 1,600 families in the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency will receive RM150 vouchers in conjunction with Deepavali to help ease their cost of living and cover preparations for the festival.
Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the first phase of distribution began yesterday evening, involving more than 300 recipients, while the remaining vouchers would be distributed at several other locations in the constituency tonight.
"They can redeem these vouchers at several supermarkets within the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency.
"I hope this will help them prepare for and celebrate Deepavali in a joyful atmosphere, while easing some of the cost-of-living pressures by helping them purchase essential items," he told reporters after the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency's Deepavali aid presentation ceremony yesterday.
On initiatives announced in Budget 2027, Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the MADANI government had provided various allocations and targeted assistance to empower the socioeconomic status of the Indian community in the country.
He said the Budget allocated RM150 million in business financing through Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) and Tekun Nasional, as well as RM150 million for the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra).
"We believe these measures can help, particularly for small business owners. They can use the funds to get their businesses up and running, purchase equipment and meet other needs, subject to the eligibility criteria set by AIM and Tekun Nasional.
"Secondly, there is the RM150 million allocation for Mitra. This is also an increase. Much of the feedback I received concerned applications for grants or assistance from Mitra. This involves access; I will convey this feedback to Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, the minister responsible for Mitra," he said.
Apart from funding and financing for entrepreneurs, Fahmi said the welfare of the Indian community was also supported through direct benefits, including Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) and assistance to repair Tamil national-type schools (SJKT).
Meanwhile, Fahmi said he had obtained approval from the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) to replace the faulty lift at the AC4 Flat in Taman Sri Sentosa, with work scheduled to begin early next year.

Title: Egypt releases prominent journalist Lina Attalah from custody
Article:
CAIRO: Egyptian authorities released independent journalist Lina Attalah from custody on Tuesday, hours after she was detained and a court ordered her website shut, her lawyer told AFP.
Attalah is one of Egypt's most prominent journalists, and her detention had sparked swift condemnation from rights groups and press freedom advocates.
A court had earlier fined Attalah three million Egyptian pounds (around US$53,400) for operating website Mada Masr without a licence, the maximum possible penalty for the misdemeanour she was charged with, and ordered the website's closure.
"Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine," her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari said, referring to a three million Egyptian pound (US$53,400) fine.
"In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds," he told AFP.
Attalah's defence team has appealed that sentence, and a new court hearing is scheduled for Nov 11, Azhari said.
News of the release followed condemnation by rights groups of the detention, which they described as a sharp escalation in Cairo's crackdown on press freedom.
Mada Masr says it has not received a response from authorities about its licence application since 2023.
The hours-long detention comes weeks after the arrest of an entire fact-checking newsroom on charges of fake news, which are frequently levelled against media seen as critical of the government.
Hossam Bahgat, head of prominent rights group the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR), was present at the court and gave AFP an account of events leading up to the arrest.
During Tuesday's hearing, the defence team said the judge ordered the room cleared except for Attalah and her lawyers, before security officers also entered the room.
Attalah's eight-person defence team had made procedural requests that were denied by the court, which then announced it had appointed its own lawyer for the journalist.
"In a move that astonished all those present, the judge recorded in the official court minutes that the court had appointed a lawyer from the Lawyers' Syndicate to represent the defence," Bahgat said.
"Lina herself spoke up to object to this lawyer being appointed to represent her, which the judge refused to record in the court minutes."
"In an even more shocking turn, the judge proceeded to dictate motions on behalf of this lawyer – who had not uttered a single word – and entered them into the official record," he added.
The judge then announced the fine and ordered Mada Masr's closure "amid shouts and protests from the defence", before security personnel in the room detained Attalah.
'Wiping out' free press
This was the sixth case brought against Attalah and Mada Masr in as many years, but none had ever gone to trial.
Egypt is currently holding 26 journalists in connection with their work, according to an EIPR tally.
The crackdown "can only mean that Egypt's security agencies are moving from years of harassing independent media to wiping them out completely", Bahgat had told AFP when Attalah was referred to trial.
Reporters Without Borders (RSF) branded the court's decision "outrageous" and "shameful", urging authorities to release Attalah "at once".
The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) also condemned the verdict.
"If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe," CPJ regional director Sara Qudah said in a statement.
Earlier this month, six journalists from fact-checking platform Matsadaash were charged with terrorism offences after being arrested in a series of raids in September.
EIPR, which represents the journalists, said they had reported torture following their arrests, allegations denied by the interior ministry.
Authorities accused them of links to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood and spreading "rumours and false news" to undermine confidence in state institutions and incite people to protest.
They are currently being held in pretrial detention, which rights groups say can be extended for months or years before detainees are released or face trial.

Title: US says will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro, family
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US State Department will issue visas to defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family, allowing them to enter the US, a senior State Department official said on Tuesday, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The official confirmed the decision in response to an inquiry from Anadolu.
The statement came amid reports that Bolsonaro had left Brazil for the United States despite a judicial travel ban.
Brazilian authorities have not confirmed his departure, and conflicting reports have emerged over his whereabouts and whether he may have attempted to travel through Argentina.
Bolsonaro, who denies any wrongdoing, is reportedly under investigation in cases involving suspected money laundering and currency evasion, as well as the financing of a biographical film about his father, former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indian court allows actor Imran Khan to stay until Nov 2
Article:
MUMBAI: An Indian court has allowed Bollywood actor Imran Khan to remain in the country until at least Nov 2, local media reported on Tuesday, suspending a government order requiring him to leave for allegedly breaching immigration laws by participating in a protest.
Khan, 43, is a US citizen and was asked to leave the country by Oct 28 after he was accused of joining protests in Mumbai against the country's election chief this month.
Under Indian law, the participation of foreigners in political protests can be treated as a violation of immigration and visa rules.
Khan appealed against the order in the Bombay High Court, saying it was unconstitutional and arbitrary, local media reported.
There was no evidence to show that Khan had participated in the protest and mobilised a crowd, his lawyer said in the appeal, legal website Live Law reported.
On Tuesday, the Bombay High Court postponed the hearing to Nov 2 for technical reasons and said the order Khan had challenged would remain on hold until then, legal website Bar and Bench posted on X.
There has been no official statement from Mumbai Police on Khan's case. The city's police chief did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.
A nephew of actor Aamir Khan, Imran belongs to a prominent film family. He acted in several hit Bollywood films from 2008 to 2015 before suddenly retiring.
His partner, Lekha Washington, said in a post on her Instagram page on Oct 12 that she, Khan, his mother and a cousin had walked towards the protest site to ask about a friend who had been detained by police and were immediately surrounded by media representatives.
"He (Imran) responded to the questions of the media, saying we have no demands, we are not part of an organisation," Washington said in the post.
Both Khan and Washington posted pictures from inside what appeared to be a police van on the day of the protests, smiling into the camera.
The rally in Mumbai was one of several protests across the country demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over what opposition parties and activists say is a revision of voter lists that benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cyclone Arnab begins making landfall in India's Andhra Pradesh state
Article:
BHUBANESWAR: A severe cyclone began making landfall in India's Andhra Pradesh state in the early hours of Wednesday, bringing high-speed winds and heavy rain that uprooted trees and disrupted power supplies, authorities said.
Thousands of people were evacuated along India's eastern coast this week, and some train and flight services were cancelled ahead of Cyclone Arnab's arrival.
The India Meteorological Department said wind speeds over the landfall area were forecast to reach 125-135km/h, with gusts of up to 150kph, over the next four hours before decreasing gradually.
A storm surge of 1.5 to 2.5 metres above the normal tide was very likely to inundate low-lying areas of Andhra Pradesh over the next six hours, the IMD said.
No loss of life had been reported so far, although trees had been uprooted in several places and power supplies disrupted, the office of Andhra Pradesh's chief minister said.
Arnab is sweeping in from the Bay of Bengal, a major region for tropical cyclones that has spawned deadly storms along India's east coast.
A super cyclone that killed nearly 10,000 people when it hit Odisha in October 1999 remains one of the country's deadliest natural disasters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Special delivery? Man nabbed over cannabis and drug-laced vapes at Kelantan courier outlet
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 28 — The General Operations Force (GOF) arrested a man, 30, in the parking lot of the Rantau Panjang Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex early yesterday to assist investigations into a drug seizure at a courier premises in Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas, on Sunday.
GOF Tenggara Brigade Commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the suspect is believed to be linked to the seizure of three kilogrammes of cannabis, 56 grammes of cannabis flowers and 10 boxes of electronic cigarettes containing cannabis oil at a Line Clear Express courier premises.
The suspect also pointed out a silver Toyota Camry believed to be used for illicit activities located five metres from where he was arrested and claimed that he was contacted by an individual to help send packages to the courier premises.
“Checks of the suspect’s body did not lead to the discovery of anything illegal, but the suspect tested positive for amphetamine,” he said in a statement yesterday, adding that the car worth RM50,000 was seized.
The suspect was arrested under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 and was handed over to the Pasir Mas district police headquarters narcotics crime investigations department for further investigation, he added. — Bernama

Title: Kedah Fire Dept says ‘Bomba’ vehicle allegedly caught running red light is not its own
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 28 — The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) has confirmed that a private vehicle bearing the word “Bomba” and equipped with a beacon light is neither an official department vehicle nor one belonging to any Volunteer Fire Brigade (PBS) in the state.
In a statement today, the department said it was aware of a video circulating on social media showing the vehicle and that further action was being taken to address the misuse of the department’s identity.
“The Kedah JBPM takes a serious view of any unauthorised use of the department’s identity, which could mislead the public and undermine the image and credibility of the fire service,” the statement said.
The department also urged the public not to speculate or disseminate unverified information that could cause confusion.
It expressed appreciation to members of the public who had provided information on the matter, stressing that public cooperation was essential to ensuring the accuracy and authenticity of information circulated.
“The Kedah JBPM remains committed to upholding the integrity and professionalism of the department while maintaining public trust in the fire service,” it added.
Previously, a five-second video went viral on social media showing a private vehicle bearing the word “Bomba” and fitted with a warning light allegedly nearly colliding with several other vehicles after running a red light in Sungai Petani. — Bernama

Title: Don’t just use technology, create it: Malaysia must step up innovation drive, says Mosti
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Malaysia must accelerate and strengthen its science, technology and innovation (STI) efforts to move beyond being a technology user and become a developer and commercialiser of homegrown technologies, said Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang.
He said the ability to develop local technologies was crucial to enhancing the country’s competitiveness and driving innovation-led economic growth amid rapid global technological advances.
Chang said this required a whole-of-nation approach, with close cooperation between the federal and state governments to strengthen the STI ecosystem, develop local talent and expand technology adoption based on each state’s needs and economic potential.
He was speaking at the Second 2026 Meeting of Ministers and State Executive Councillors Responsible for Science, Technology and Innovation (MEXCO-STI) here yesterday.
Chang said MEXCO-STI provided an important platform to align policies, strategies and implementation of the national STI agenda between the federal and state governments.
The meeting also discussed measures to address challenges arising from Malaysia’s expected transition to an ageing nation by 2048.
The Malaysian Innovation Foundation (YIM) presented initiatives combining STI to empower older people, develop high-tech businesses and preserve and commercialise traditional knowledge.
Another focus was the use of a circular economy to generate income for fishermen. The programme, introduced by Bioeconomy Corporation (BEC), is expected to cover at least 30 identified locations across Peninsular Malaysia in 2027.
Meanwhile, Chang said the ministry (Mosti) was coordinating preparations for the Second 2026 National Science Council (MSN) meeting, scheduled for Nov 24 and to be chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the views and proposals raised at MEXCO-STI would also be brought to the council meeting to help strengthen the country’s STI policies and development direction.
On efforts to nurture interest in STI among the public, Chang said Mosti’s Malaysia Techlympics programme had reached 3.18 million young people nationwide, surpassing its original target of 1.8 million participants.
He said the achievement reflected growing interest in STI among young people, supported by state governments and other stakeholders.
On innovation commercialisation, Chang said the National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo (NICE) 2026 attracted more than 12,000 visitors, with 180 exhibitors and 235 business-matching sessions.
However, he stressed that the success of the country’s innovation ecosystem should be measured not merely by programme participation but by its ability to commercialise research, create new economic opportunities and deliver tangible benefits to the public.
He said stronger coordination between the federal and state governments was essential to ensure STI investments, expertise and infrastructure were used effectively, without duplication or waste of resources. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya still working on loophole in planned road crash payouts: What if offenders have no money?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Bereaved families who lose a breadwinner to reckless or drunk drivers could soon secure direct compensation through criminal courts, but the federal government is still working out how awards will be collected if the convicted motorist possesses no financial means.
The Transport Ministry is preparing amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 to establish a statutory compensation framework for victims and lawful heirs in road crashes resulting in death or grievous hurt, according to a written parliamentary reply tabled in the Dewan Rakyat.
Responding to a query from Setiu MP Shaharizukirnain Abd. Kadir, the ministry said that Putrajaya favours judicial discretion over fixed administrative payout caps.
Under the envisioned framework, criminal trial judges would order convicted motorists to pay restitution assessed on case merits, factoring in the severity of injuries, the tangible economic loss suffered by dependants, and the offender's financial standing.
However, tailoring compensation to an offender's personal wealth exposes a major enforcement loophole, as impoverished or unhedged drivers may be unable to settle substantial awards. The ministry acknowledged this structural hurdle, confirming that technical working groups are examining recovery mechanisms.
“The government is also examining the question of the offender’s ability to pay compensation, the method of payment, and enforcement of the order if the offender lacks sufficient assets or financial means.
“This is important to ensure that compensation orders are not only legally authorised but actually benefit victims and heirs,” the ministry said.
Without a state-backed insolvency guarantee or an integrated insurance recovery mechanism, legal experts note that restitution orders risk becoming hollow paper judgments.
For lower-income households that rely entirely on a single breadwinner, the sudden loss of an income earner delivers immediate financial destitution that paper awards cannot relieve.
The ministry stressed that justice for crash victims must extend beyond penal incarceration to address the economic fallout endured by surviving dependants.
It noted that inter-agency consultations with relevant ministries and legal stakeholders are ongoing to finalise the mechanism.

Title: Kuching North achieves Level 1 Smart City status, now sets sights on Level 2
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 28 — Kuching North has achieved Smart City Level 1 under the Smart City Rating Criteria set by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), with efforts now geared towards meeting the requirements for Level 2.
Caretaker Minister in the Premier’s Department Datuk Dr Abdul Rahman Junaidi said the achievement reflected Kuching North City Commission’s (DBKU) continued efforts to strengthen urban governance through technology and innovation.
In his welcoming speech at the Sarawak Urban Forum 2.0 here on Monday, he said DBKU had been strengthening its smart city agenda through the digitalisation of services and adoption of technology to improve the efficiency of urban management.
“Through the i-DBKU platform, DBKU continues to expand digital service delivery to provide more efficient, integrated and people-friendly services,” he said.
Among the smart city initiatives implemented by DBKU are smart street lighting, smart traffic lights, Geographic Information System, and closed-circuit television systems.
Dr Abdul Rahman also highlighted DBKU’s strategic collaboration with the Malaysian Space Agency through a memorandum of understanding, which opens up opportunities to use space technology and satellite data for urban management, environmental monitoring, land-use planning, and disaster management.
He said the collaboration demonstrated the potential of technology to improve urban planning and management while helping the city prepare for future challenges.
“A future-ready city is not determined solely by the modernity of its infrastructure, sophistication of its technology or economic growth.
“Rather, it is a city that can anticipate change, address challenges effectively, adapt to new circumstances and ensure its people continue to enjoy a high quality of life,” he said.
He said cities today face various challenges such as climate change, waste management, urban mobility, environmental sustainability and digital transformation.
“Therefore, we must ensure that urban development is carried out in a balanced manner, alongside heritage preservation, environmental protection and community well-being,” he added.
On Kuching’s development, Dr Abdul Rahman said the city should continue to modernise while preserving its historical identity and cultural uniqueness.
Progress, he stressed, must benefit all segments of society without neglecting the interests of future generations.
He added that urban development should not be measured solely by the number of buildings constructed, infrastructure improvements or economic growth, but also by the quality of life, community well-being and the ability to meet the needs of present and future generations. — The Borneo Post

Title: Life after the military: Nearly 800 veterans find new careers beyond the uniform through Kerjaya Kedua Perwira initiative, says Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — A total of 1,409 prospective retirees and veterans of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) have benefited from the Kerjaya Kedua Perwira initiative under the Perhebat Transformation Plan as of September, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
He said that of the total, 781 veterans had successfully secured employment in high-value sectors, including aerospace, automotive, logistics and services, with average salaries ranging from RM2,970 to RM5,000.
“Meanwhile, 628 prospective MAF retirees are undergoing industry-based training,” he said at the 71st Convocation Ceremony of the Armed Forces Ex-Servicemen Affairs Corporation (Perhebat) at Dewan Jubli Perak, Perhebat Complex, Sungai Buloh Camp, near here, yesterday.
The text of his speech was read out by the Ministry of Defence’s deputy secretary-general (Management), Datin Roszanina Wahab.
Mohamed Khaled said Perhebat must remain proactive in enhancing the skills, competencies and employability of service personnel and veterans to enable them to pursue high-value career opportunities.
“Many of them retire in their 40s while they are still energetic and capable of working, and we should not allow their potential to go to waste.
“I urge those nearing retirement who are still able to work not to rest for too long after the transition period, but to make use of the opportunities available to find suitable employment after retirement,” he said.
Meanwhile, Perhebat director-general Datuk Amir Md Noor said the corporation remained committed to developing a high-performing workforce as a key asset in supporting the Madani economic development agenda, with strong industry participation through the Kerjaya Kedua Perwira initiative.
“To date, Perhebat has collaborated with 513 agencies and private companies across various industries to help this group secure jobs that match their skills,” he said.
He said the close partnerships had enabled Perhebat to prepare the first cohort of veterans to take on operational roles with the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL).
Amir said 10 participants in the East Coast Rail Link Industrial Skills Training Programme (PLKI-ECRL) had successfully completed a one-year course at Liuzhou Railway Vocational Technical College in China.
“Perhebat will continue to strengthen an integrated ecosystem linking prospective retirees and MAF veterans with industry and the job market, allowing them to use their experience, skills and competencies to continue contributing to national development while enhancing their well-being,” he said.
A total of 4,164 MAF personnel from across the country were recognised at the convocation ceremony after successfully completing their transition training.
As of September, 833 MAF personnel and veterans had been awarded the Malaysian Skills Advanced Diploma, Malaysian Skills Diploma and Malaysian Skills Certificate through the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) programme. — Bernama

Title: What went wrong at sea? MMEA to review SOPs after fatal Perlis boat pursuit
Article:
KUALA NERANG, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) will conduct an internal investigation into a boat collision that claimed the life of one of its personnel in waters off Perlis two days ago.
MMEA Deputy Director-General (Operations) Maritime Vice-Admiral Mohd Zawawi Abdullah said the investigation would focus on identifying weaknesses and determining whether the agency’s standard operating procedures (SOPs) needed improvement to prevent similar incidents.
“For every operation, the MMEA has specific SOPs in place, and our personnel are constantly reminded to comply with them.
“Whenever an incident occurs, a post-mortem or internal investigation is conducted to identify shortcomings that can be addressed through improvements,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the funeral of Senior Maritime Petty Officer (Technical) Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, at the Muslim cemetery of Masjid Tengku Sarafudin Badlishah here last night.
Mohd Zawawi said the investigation would also examine other areas for improvement, including personnel training and the equipment used during operations.
“Such internal investigations are usually initiated as soon as possible and may take a few weeks to complete.
“We want to determine whether any SOPs need to be refined for the benefit of all MMEA personnel and to prevent similar incidents from recurring,” he added.
He stressed that the incident would not dampen the morale of MMEA personnel but would instead strengthen their resolve, particularly among those serving on the front lines, to remain committed to safeguarding the nation’s maritime security.
On the welfare of the deceased’s family, Mohd Zawawi said the agency would ensure that his widow and two school-going children received appropriate assistance in accordance with existing procedures.
Mohd Roshaimi was killed while three other MMEA personnel were injured when the boat they were in reportedly struck a concrete structure in waters off Kuala Sungai Padang, near Kuala Perlis, at about 11 pm on Monday.
The personnel were pursuing a boat suspected of carrying undocumented migrants when the incident occurred. — Bernama

Title: Pay-as-you-drive insurance being studied to lower costs for e-hailing drivers, Transport Ministry says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The federal government is studying dynamic insurance and takaful models that price coverage based on mileage and driver risk profiles, seeking to rein in escalating vehicle operating costs across the e-hailing industry.
In a written reply yesterday to Bakri MP Tan Hong Pin in the Dewan Rakyat, the Transport Ministry confirmed that a dedicated Inter-Agency Task Force (IATF) convened by Bank Negara Malaysia is spearheading efforts to restructure e-hailing insurance mechanisms and alleviate the financial burden on drivers.
Under the framework being considered, traditional fixed annual premiums could make way for usage-based policies calculated on a per-kilometre basis alongside individual risk ratings.
The ministry explained that aligning pricing directly with actual road time and trip volume is intended to create fairer, more responsive coverage tailored to the varying work patterns of gig-economy motorists.
The task force is also evaluating the integration of telematics technology, which monitors driving habits such as speed, acceleration, and braking patterns, to incentivise safer road behaviour and mitigate crash risks.
Concurrently, the government is exploring deeper data-sharing protocols between e-hailing platform operators and underwriters to improve risk assessment accuracy and streamline accident claims verification.
