The long-term reform brings together the Transport Ministry, Bank Negara, the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD), the Road Transport Department (JPJ), insurance and takaful providers, and e-hailing driver associations under a coordinated inter-agency framework.
The ministry reiterated that valid motor insurance remains a strict statutory obligation under Section 90(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, enforced by JPJ to ensure financial indemnification for drivers, passengers, and third parties involved in road traffic collisions.
Wider social safety protections for the gig sector remain distinct from vehicular coverage, falling under the purview of the Human Resources Ministry through the Employees' Social Security Act 1969, the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017, and the Gig Workers Act 2025.
However, the parliamentary reply stopped short of committing to an implementation timeline or projecting the expected percentage drop in premium expenses for drivers.

Title: A father’s final farewell: Jalur Gemilang presented as MMEA officer killed at sea laid to rest in Kedah
Article:
KUALA NERANG, Oct 28 — The remains of Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer Technical Leading Seaman Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, who died in a boat collision in Perlis waters yesterday, were laid to rest last night.
The burial at Masjid Tengku Sarafudin Badlishah Islamic Cemetery here was completed at 9.45pm, with the MMEA conducting funeral rites and providing a ceremonial escort as a final tribute to the deceased.
Earlier, the remains arrived at the mosque at 8.41pm from Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital in Alor Setar after the post-mortem examination was completed.
Funeral prayers were held at the mosque, led by Mohd Izhar Zakaria, and attended by hundreds of congregants, including family members, locals and MMEA personnel.
The remains were then taken to the mosque cemetery, where about 500 people attended the funeral.
After the funeral, MMEA deputy director-general (Operations) Vice-Admiral (Maritime) Mohd Zawawi Abdullah presented the Jalur Gemilang to the deceased’s father.
Also present were Kedah and Perlis MMEA director First Admiral (Maritime) Romli Mustafa and dozens of MMEA personnel.
In the incident at about 11pm on Monday, Mohd Roshaimi was killed while three other officers were injured after the boat they were travelling in was believed to have struck a concrete structure in the waters off Kuala Sungai Padang, near Kuala Perlis, while pursuing a boat suspected of carrying illegal immigrants. — Bernama

Title: JCorp hits back at Indonesian forest fire claims, says plantation ties ended years ago
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Johor Corporation (JCorp) yesterday refuted claims associating the group with Indonesian plantation companies linked to forest and land fires, following a recent report published by Wahana Linkungan Hidup Indonesia (WALHI).
In a statement yesterday, JCorp clarified that it does not own or operate any plantation outside Malaysia.
JCorp further explained that through its wholly owned subsidiary, Kulim (Malaysia) Berhad (Kulim), it divested its interests in several Indonesian companies in 2007.
The disposals involved PT Graha Cakra Mulia, PT Sumber Mahardhika Graha, PT Salonok Ladang Mas, and PT Harapan Hibrida Kalbar on August 8, 2007, followed by PT Trimurti Sumbertama on September 26, 2007, with all disposals recorded in JCorp’s 2008 Annual Report.
JCorp added that on July 6, 2023, Kulim further divested its entire equity interest in two other entities, PT Tempirai Palm Resources and PT Rambang Agro Jaya to PT Bakung Starch Lestari.
JCorp reiterated that it has no ownership interest or operational involvement in these companies.
Consequently, the group noted that the continued publication and circulation of these unfounded claims, create a false impression that JCorp owns, controls or operates the companies involved, associating it with the alleged incidents.
“As a state-owned institution, these unwarranted insinuations cause serious reputational harm to JCorp and the Johor State Government,” the statement said.
JCorp is a value driven organisation with total assets exceeding RM26 billion as at end FY2025.
JCorp’s flagship companies; KPJ Healthcare Berhad, JLand Group Sdn Bhd, Johor Plantations Group Berhad, QSR Brands (M) Holdings Bhd and Johor Capital Group Sdn Bhd, spearhead the Group’s interests across five core sectors namely Wellness & Healthcare, Real Estate & Infrastructure, Agribusiness, Food & Restaurant, and Patient Capital.
Recently the analysis by Indonesian environmental non-governmental organisation, WALHI claims that 21 companies linked to Malaysian business entities were involved in land and forest fires in Indonesia between January and September 2026.
The details were highlighted in a mapping report titled “Who Are Behind the Fires?” published by the organisation’s National Executive. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman CID takes over custodial death probe after forensic examination reveals blunt-force injuries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly while in police custody has been taken over by the Prosecution/Legal Division (D5) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) at Bukit Aman.
Bukit Aman CID director Datuk M. Kumar said the case is now being investigated under Section 331 of the Penal Code, on intentional infliction of grievous hurt to extort a confession or to compel the restoration of property.
He explained that this classification was determined following a statement recorded by a forensic medical consultant at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz who conducted the post-mortem, confirmed the presence of external injuries on several parts of the deceased’s body.
The pattern of these injuries is consistent with blunt-force trauma and was not self-inflicted.
“However, the complete post-mortem report confirming the cause of death has yet to be obtained, and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is awaiting further information from the hospital regarding this matter,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Kumar added that the investigation is ongoing to identify the police officers and personnel involved in the handling and management of the victim while he was in custody at Cheras district police headquarters.
“The investigation will be conducted thoroughly and professionally, without any element of a ‘cover-up,’ to ensure that criminal justice is upheld in accordance with the prevailing laws,” he asserted.
He further emphasised that PDRM is committed to ensuring transparency and integrity throughout the investigation, guaranteeing impartial justice for all, and will not compromise on any form of misconduct. — Bernama

Title: ‘Corporate Mafia’ probe freezes over RM400m in assets, no MACC officers implicated, Home Ministry tells Parliament
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Federal police have found no evidence linking Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officers to alleged “corporate mafia” syndicates after questioning 70 individuals in an ongoing anti-money laundering operation, the Home Ministry told the Dewan Rakyat.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the ministry confirmed that checks on those called up by investigators revealed no information to support such claims.
“Based on the background and identities of the witnesses called for statement recording, no MACC officers were involved or identified for the purpose of assisting the investigation.
“At present, the Op Viking investigation is continuing in order to complete the entire investigation paper. The Ministry gives an assurance that PDRM is committed to carrying out this investigation in accordance with the laws in force,” the ministry said.
The disclosure came in response to Pengkalan Chepa MP Datuk Dr Ahmad Marzuk Shaary, who asked the home minister to outline the status of the investigation, clarify whether MACC or other regulatory officials were being probed for abuse of power, and detail progress following a Cabinet directive ordering a comprehensive inquiry.
The high-level investigation stems from a Bloomberg report published on Feb 12, 2026, which alleged the existence of an entrenched “corporate mafia” in Malaysia. The report claimed rogue elements within regulatory and enforcement bodies abused their statutory powers to intimidate corporate executives into selling company equity at depressed prices, enabling third-party syndicates to engineer hostile corporate takeovers.
In response, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) launched Op Viking through its specialized Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) criminal investigation division, opening formal investigation papers on Oct 14, 2025, under Section 4(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
As part of the nationwide operation, investigators have detained several individuals and moved aggressively against suspected proceeds of crime.
As of Sept 25, 2026, police had recorded statements from 70 individuals while freezing or seizing assets exceeding RM409 million.
The frozen assets include 417 central depository system (CDS) accounts and 70 share-trading portfolios valued at roughly RM323.59 million, alongside 404 bank accounts holding a combined RM85.62 million. Officers also seized eight real estate properties and 11 vehicles linked to the probe.
The ministry stated that police are actively pursuing remaining operational leads to finalise the investigation papers for prosecutorial review.
However, the parliamentary reply did not specify whether any of the 70 questioned individuals have been designated as formal criminal suspects, whether charges are pending, or if personnel from other regulatory agencies remain under scrutiny.
The ministry also refrained from identifying the registered owners of the impounded equity and bank accounts, with asset freezes under AMLA serving as an investigative safeguard rather than a legal finding of guilt.

Title: WCE heading south? Zahid says Banting-Masjid Tanah extension a priority, Johor next on the cards
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 28 — The extension of the West Coast Expressway (WCE) from Banting, Selangor, to Masjid Tanah was among the matters discussed by the Cabinet, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said if realised, this new highway alignment would not only alleviate traffic congestion but also serve as a catalyst for economic growth in the areas affected by the project.
“Currently, the completed alignment stretches from Taiping to Banting, Selangor. Moving forward, God willing, the route from Banting to Masjid Tanah, continuing toward Batu Pahat and Pontian, will pass through Masjid Tanah.
“Datuk Rauf (Chief Minister)… this is what we discussed previously. The West Coast Expressway will not only cover Pontian, Batu Pahat, and Muar, it will also reach Masjid Tanah. We will prioritise the section from Masjid Tanah to Banting, God willing,” he said.
He made these remarks while speaking at the launch of the Barisan Nasional election machinery for the Masjid Tanah parliamentary constituency here last night.
Earlier, the Melaka state government had reportedly requested that the Federal Government consider the development of a new WCE alignment, running from Banting through Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan, before entering Melaka and continuing into Johor.
The proposed expansion of the highway is seen as having the potential to improve connectivity, stimulate industrial and tourism activities, and create new economic growth opportunities for the local population. — Bernama

Title: Open-channel admissions won’t reduce UPU quotas at public universities, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) has stressed that offering admission to public universities through the open channel will not affect or reduce the quota allocated through UPU, Malaysia’s centralised university admissions system.
Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said open channel admissions accounted for only a small percentage and were limited to specific courses with available places, rather than being intended solely to generate revenue for the institutions.
“I would like to inform this House that this issue does not arise at all, as we will maintain the quotas that have been set,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage for the ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
On differences in tuition fees, Zambry acknowledged that they existed, particularly for critical courses.
However, he said the government continued to take initiatives to increase allocations and quotas for critical courses such as accounting, engineering and artificial intelligence (AI) to accommodate the high number of qualified students.
Zambry also said that poverty or financial constraints should not be a reason for students to turn down offers to study at public universities, as various forms of financial assistance were available.
“The government provides various forms of financial support covering tuition fees and living allowances, including the Community College Student Financial Assistance, Foundation Financial Assistance and B40 TVET Scholarships,” he said.
Meanwhile, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, when winding up the debate for his ministry, said Malaysia recorded 32.26 million international visitor arrivals from January to September 2026, an increase of 2.4 per cent compared with the same period last year.
He said the government continued to intensify tourism promotion efforts using existing allocations to sustain the industry’s growth momentum, particularly in facing global geopolitical challenges that affected visitors’ travel plans.
Tiong said that, to improve international connectivity, Tourism Malaysia had worked with 24 airlines, comprising three domestic and 21 international carriers, to support 46 international flight routes from January to October this year.
“Of these, 35 were new routes while the remaining 11 were existing routes that continued to operate. They included Xi’an-Kuala Lumpur, Guiyang-Kuala Lumpur, Shanghai-Tawau, Xiamen-Kota Kinabalu, Busan-Kuala Lumpur and Frankfurt-Kuala Lumpur, as well as charter flights from Warsaw, Poland, and Almaty, Kazakhstan, scheduled for December,” he said.
He said the business events segment, including meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE), also performed encouragingly, with its economic impact rising 113.7 per cent to RM1.24 billion in the second quarter of 2026. The number of events increased 81.2 per cent to 125, while international delegate attendance rose 105.2 per cent to 83,596.
To strengthen growth in the segment, Tiong said RM10 million had been allocated to the Malaysia Convention and Exhibition Bureau (MyCEB) to attract more high-impact MICE and international sporting events. Tax incentives for organising international-standard events had also been extended for the 2028-2030 period.
Meanwhile, Deputy Dewan Rakyat Speaker Datuk Seri Ramli Mohd Nor expressed his appreciation to the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (Motac) for its cooperation in organising the Sewang Festival, which brought together 18 Orang Asli ethnic groups on October 24.
He said the event had the potential to attract international tourists and was targeted to be held at the national level next year.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting resumes today. — Bernama

Title: Tiger on the prowl? Suspected paw prints found near Gerik homes, Perhilitan trap activated
Article:
IPOH, Oct 28 — The Perak Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) has confirmed the discovery of footprints believed to belong to a tiger at Felda Lepang Nenering in Pengkalan Hulu, Gerik, on October 26.
Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah said the confirmation was made following an investigation and field inspection by the Gerik District Perhilitan Office after it received a report from a plantation worker about the incident on the same day.
“For now, Perhilitan has activated a tiger trap located less than a kilometre from where the footprints were found.
“We believe the tiger ventured close to the plantation and residential areas because Felda Lepang Nenering is located near the Bintang Hijau Permanent Forest Reserve,” he told Bernama when contacted yesterday.
Earlier, several photographs showing the discovery of the predator’s footprints went viral on Facebook, prompting various reactions and raising concerns among social media users.
Pazil also denied claims by some members of the public that reports about the presence of a tiger in the area had been made long ago, but Perhilitan had taken no action.
“We did not receive any recent official report of a tiger sighting before October 26. Records show that the last report concerning the species at Felda Lepang Nenering was received on July 30,” he said.
He said Perhilitan would continue monitoring the area and had also disseminated safety guidelines to plantation workers to prevent any untoward incidents.
In a related development, he said 26 reports of human-tiger conflict had been recorded in the Hulu Perak district from January to date, and appropriate action had been taken on all of them. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan eyes more seats beyond defending incumbents, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) aims to retain its existing seats and targets to wrest potentially winnable seats in the Melaka state election, said PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The communications minister said the matter was among those discussed at the PH presidential council meeting held yesterday evening to fine-tune preparations for the coalition’s election machinery.
“Our baseline is the seats we want to retain. At the same time, we are looking for opportunities to wrest several seats. If our efforts and strategies are properly executed, it is not impossible for us to bring about a change.
“We have our targets, but we are realistic and understand the situation. Nevertheless, we see several factors that could enable the seats we are targeting to swing to Pakatan Harapan,” he told reporters after the presentation of the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency Deepavali contributions here last night.
On preparations by the election machinery, Fahmi said the Presidential Council had been briefed by Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari and Melaka PKR State Leadership Council (MPN) acting chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim on the state-level readiness.
“As for the candidates announced recently, I can see that they are continuing their groundwork, and we believe that by the nomination day on October 31, Insya-Allah, PH candidates will be ready to face those contesting in the Melaka state election,” he said.
Apart from the Melaka state polls, he said the PH Presidential Council meeting was also briefed on the dissolution of the Sarawak state legislative assembly and several initiatives for the implementation of government reforms.
Meanwhile, on facilities for media personnel covering the Melaka state polls, Fahmi said a main media centre operated by the Information Department would begin operations from October 30 to November 14 at Hotel Mudzaffar, Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf claims progress in MCA seat talks despite Wee Ka Siong’s reservations
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 28 — Discussions between Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh and MCA President Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong is believed to have successfully resolved several deadlocks regarding seat distribution for the Melaka state election (PRN) next month.
Ab Rauf, who is also the Melaka BN election director, described the development as “positive” when met by reporters.
“(The discussion was) good, great... we managed to resolve the deadlocks that had previously arisen. We will wait for MCA itself to later perhaps provide the outcome (decision) from the negotiations I discussed with him (MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong) (on Monday) night,” he said.
He spoke to reporters after the Launching the Masjid Tanah Parliamentary BN Machinery, officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also BN chairman, in Masjid Tanah here last night.
Earlier, Wee was reported to have said in a Facebook post yesterday that MCA and Umno had not reconnected following a meeting at a hotel in Kuala Lumpur on Monday night.
He was quoted as saying that it was too early for Ahmad Zahid to describe the outcome of the meeting as positive, adding that both sides need to continue discussions to reach a resolution in the near future.
Previously, MCA reportedly stated that it would not recognise any candidates from the party announced by BN for the Melaka state election without the approval of its top leadership.
Wee said the act of announcing candidates without consultation and agreement from MCA was unacceptable, especially when seats previously contested by MCA were allegedly given to other parties.
Last Saturday, BN announced the coalition’s candidates contesting 21 state legislative assembly (DUN) seats, including two MCA candidates: incumbent Machap Jaya assemblyman Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem and incumbent Kelebang assemblyman Datuk Lim Ban Hong. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Respect Pakatan’s decision to give Bemban seat to Bersatu, Amirudin tells dissenters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) component parties must respect the coalition’s decision to hand the Bemban state seat to a Bersatu candidate in the Melaka state election, says PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said party members must respect the consensus reached by the coalition and their respective leaderships regarding electoral pacts and seat allocations.
He said PH maintains an open approach to discussions, considering every possibility in determining the direction of its political partnerships.
“This is PH’s decision, and all party members should respect the coalition’s collective choice. In PH, we discuss matters openly, weighing all possibilities and probabilities,” he told reporters after opening the Gombak-Hulu Langat Geopark 2026 Re-evaluation Session at the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council (MPAJ) Convention Centre here yesterday.
Last Saturday, former Melaka DAP chairman Damian Yeo was reported to have said he was willing to quit politics rather than support PH’s move to hand over the Bemban seat to a Bersatu candidate in the state polls.
The former Duyong assemblyman reportedly cited past political betrayals that made it difficult to accept any proposed cooperation with Bersatu.
Meanwhile, Amirudin, who is also a PKR vice-president, said any decision to extend electoral pacts with Bersatu to the Sarawak state election or the 16th General Election (GE16) has not been finalised.
“So far, we have not been tested yet, and we will see what the outcome is after the Melaka state election,” he said.
On political ties between PH and Bersatu in Selangor, Amirudin said no decision has been reached, pending further deliberations.
“We will wait because it involves lengthy discussions. God willing, we will make a decision soon, possibly during or after the election,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Tragic discovery: Body of 14-year-old snatched by crocodile in Sarawak finally found
Article:
KUCHING, — The body of a teenage boy who was attacked by a crocodile at Ulu Sungai Plaie in Sebuyau was found on Tuesday night.
In an update at 10.13pm, the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said the 14-year-old’s body was found by villagers.
Police were sent to the location to retrieve the body and transport it to Simunjan Hospital.
The boy, identified as Mohamad Nordin Mohamad Othman, was attacked by a crocodile on Monday afternoon.
The attack occurred when the victim was loading oil palm fruits into a boat and was witnessed by his uncle. — The Borneo Post

Title: Miti: Malaysia’s exports to US surge 69pc despite tariffs, powered by AI boom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Malaysia’s exports to the United States surged 69.1 per cent to RM282.07 billion for January to September 2026, while total trade between the two countries rose 39.6 per cent to RM378.70 billion.
The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) said Malaysia’s trade performance with the US continues to grow despite its exports being subjected to additional tariffs following investigations under various legal instruments conducted by the US.
According to the ministry, the strong export performance was mainly driven by a surge in demand for electrical and electronic (E&E) products, particularly semiconductors, following rapid developments in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and data centres.
“A critical factor driving this growth is Malaysia’s strategic advantage in receiving exemptions from additional tariffs imposed by the US on most semiconductor and E&E products,” said Miti in a written response published on the Parliament’s website on Tuesday.
The ministry was responding to Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari (PH-Gombak), who sought to know the impact of US tariff impositions on Malaysia’s industry in 2026 and the new alternative markets being explored to enable micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to export their goods.
The ministry noted that the E&E sector accounts for about 64.2 per cent of Malaysia’s total exports to the US, with 44 per cent of E&E exports comprising semiconductor products.
However, Miti said that in the same period, Malaysia’s rubber glove exports to the US decreased by 1.6 per cent to RM5.0 billion, furniture exports fell by 19.2 per cent to RM3.77 billion, and medical device exports dropped by 12.0 per cent to RM8.74 billion.
He said several key Malaysian industries are under pressure to absorb US tariff costs or offer discounts to buyers to maintain product competitiveness, continue exports, and preserve access to that market.
“Miti believes that efforts to diversify markets and reduce excessive dependence on any single market are the best steps to minimise exposure to external shocks and to enhance the country’s trade resilience.
“In this regard, Miti continues to actively work to enhance market access and open new markets through various free trade agreements (FTAs) that have been signed, in addition to exploring non-traditional markets in West Asia, Africa, Latin America, and South Asia,” it added.
Meanwhile, in a separate reply to Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman (PN-Bachok), Miti said it is finalising the implementation of the New Incentive Framework (NIF) for the services sector, following its rollout for the manufacturing sector from March 1, 2026.
According to the ministry, the NIF shifts the tax incentive approach from a product- and activity-based system to a performance-based approach, with greater emphasis on outcomes and the economic impact generated by a project.
Miti said this in response to Mohd Syahir’s question about the reforms in the investment application evaluation process to ensure added value to the national economy, particularly through the creation of quality jobs. — Bernama

Title: In Dewan Rakyat today: RM20.1b 1MDB liabilities, BUDI95 quota changes and data centres under spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The status of efforts to settle 1Malaysia Development Bhd’s (1MDB) remaining net liabilities, estimated at RM20.1 billion, including assets and claims still being recovered, is among the issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper published on Parliament’s website, Lee Chuan How (PH-Ipoh Timor) will ask the finance minister to provide an update on the matter, including the amount expected to be recovered from each claim and the government’s target year for fully settling the outstanding liabilities.
Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan (PN-Permatang Pauh) will also seek an explanation from the finance minister on the rationale behind the reduction in the Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) subsidised petrol quota from 300 litres to 200 litres before it was increased again on September 1, 2026.
Other issues expected to be raised include data centre operations, plans to upgrade federal and state roads, and measures to address learning loss among pupils from hardcore poor households.
Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong) is scheduled to ask the works minister about plans to upgrade federal and state roads in Bentong to cope with increased traffic following the completion of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project.
Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal (PN-Machang) will seek details of the government’s contingency plans to ensure that data centre operations do not compromise electricity and water supplies for the public during droughts or supply disruptions.
Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar (BN-Kinabatangan) will seek clarification on the government’s strategic action plan to assist pupils from multidimensionally hardcore poor households who continue to experience long-term learning loss.
Following the question-and-answer session, the Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to resume the winding-up of the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 by the respective ministries. — Bernama

Title: As AI enters classrooms, Anwar warns against losing what makes us human
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technology are vital for the future of education; however, their use must be balanced with the cultivation of moral, human values, and character among students, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In a video shared on his Facebook page, the prime minister noted that while AI possesses capabilities in terms of knowledge and intelligence, it lacks the values, character, and humanity that must be nurtured within and embodied by human beings.
“We are moving in that direction (the use of technology), but there is a caveat, we must ‘reach for the skies while remaining rooted to the earth.’ Why? Because while AI is important, it also presents certain issues.
“It (AI) possesses knowledge, but it lacks humanity and moral depth. It has no values, no character, and no humanity. It is merely intelligence,” he said.
Anwar made these remarks in response to a student’s question regarding the possibility of all schools in the country adopting technologies such as tablets, laptops, and AI in the future.
Earlier yesterday, at the Parliament building, he met and interacted with students from schools in Pasir Gudang and Pontian, Johor.
The prime minister said the nation is indeed moving toward the integration of technology in education; however, this progress must be accompanied by an awareness of technology’s limitations and the importance of preserving human values.
Anwar emphasised that intelligence alone is insufficient if not coupled with values and character, adding that education must continue to focus on the development of a well-rounded individual.
“Is technology important? Yes, it is. A lack of intelligence is dangerous, but if we focus solely on intelligence, human values are lost.
“Therefore, as we move in that direction (the use of technology), we must remain mindful of how we can continue to stay truly human,” he said.
The prime minister also emphasised the importance of the concept of
akal budi
(intellect and moral character) within the Malay culture, which links the capacity for thought with ethical conduct, thereby demonstrating that an individual’s intelligence should not be measured solely by their knowledge.
In this regard, he encouraged students to cultivate the habit of cherishing their parents and expressing affection in their daily lives.
Anwar noted that simple gestures such as hugging and kissing one’s parents, or showing them appreciation help foster values of love and humanity. These values must be preserved, even as society continues to advance technologically.
“Could we perhaps start a new culture? Hugging and kissing one’s parents? I once saw someone return home and kiss his father; the father was puzzled, wondering, ‘What does he want from me? ‘simply because such a practice had never existed before. Show appreciation, express affection. There is absolutely no harm in it,” he said. — Bernama

Title: No decision yet on financial aid for debt-hit AirAsia, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government has yet to decide whether to provide financial support to financially distressed AirAsia Group Bhd, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
He said both the Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Finance are reviewing proposals to assist the airline.
“The government’s priority is to ensure ongoing airline operations and maintain connectivity, as the bankruptcy of a major airline would disrupt this connectivity. If an airline shuts down, it would not only result in job losses, but also affect connectivity, with adverse consequences for the country.
“This is a matter of concern to the government, and we are doing our utmost to prevent such a situation,” he told the Dewan Rakyat while winding up the debate on the Transport Ministry’s 2027 Budget yesterday.
Loke was responding to Khairil Nizam Khirudin (PN-Jerantut), who raised concerns over the low-cost carrier’s high debt and asked whether the Transport Ministry was considering assistance, citing its 26,000 employees and the potential impact on jobs. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak seeks more flights and buses to bring voters home for state election
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 28 — The Ministry of Transport Sarawak (MOTS) has written to airlines and express bus operators to explore additional services before and after polling day for the upcoming 13th Sarawak State Election.
MOTS said in a statement yesterday that the move aims to support Sarawakians returning to their registered constituencies to fulfil their civic duty.
It said the ministry recognises that many Sarawakians work in various states in Peninsular Malaysia, as well as in Singapore and Sabah, and may face challenges in arranging their journeys home during periods of high travel demand.
“For air travel, MOTS has requested airlines to plan for increased flight frequencies during the week before and the week after polling day, to accommodate voters travelling home to vote and their return journeys afterwards.
“For express bus services, MOTS has advised and encouraged operators in Sarawak to temporarily increase trip frequencies from three days before polling day until three days after polling day,” according to MOTS.
MOTS also encourages travellers to plan their journeys early and refer to operators’ official channels for accurate information on schedules, fares and bookings.
On October 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg announced that the State Legislative Assembly would be dissolved on Monday (October 26), paving the way for the 13th state election. — Bernama

Title: Parliament gets more independence: What will its new council actually do?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Parliament is expected to scrutinise government decisions, debate laws and examine how public money is spent, but who manages the institution itself?
That question is at the heart of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025, which came into force on October 1, restoring a dedicated service intended to give Parliament greater control over its staffing, finances and administration after more than three decades under the government’s administrative structure.
The law establishes the Parliamentary Service Council to oversee the service, with the aim of strengthening Parliament’s institutional independence from the executive, which refers to the prime minister, Cabinet and government ministries.
The council came into focus on October 14, when the Dewan Rakyat approved four MPs, two from the government and two from the Opposition, to sit on it.
But what does the council actually do, who sits on it, and how far does its authority extend?
Malay Mail
explains.
What is the Parliamentary Service Council?
The Parliamentary Service Council is the body responsible for matters relating to the Parliamentary Service, a separate service established under the Parliamentary Service Act 2025 (Act 869).
In practical terms, it is intended to give Parliament greater say over the staff and resources needed to carry out its work, rather than leaving these matters largely dependent on administrative arrangements within the executive.
The council does not replace Parliament or take over MPs’ responsibility for debating legislation and scrutinising the government.
Instead, it oversees the administrative machinery that supports those duties.
Who sits on the council?
The council will have 16 members drawn from Parliament and the public service.
The President of the Dewan Negara serves as chairman, while the Speaker of the Dewan Rakyat is co-chairman.
The other parliamentary members are the Deputy President of the Dewan Negara, two Deputy Speakers of the Dewan Rakyat, two senators and four MPs.
The four MPs must comprise two government representatives and two Opposition representatives.
They are nominated by the Dewan Rakyat’s Committee of Selection and approved through a resolution of the House.
The Dewan Rakyat on October 14 approved Ramkarpal Singh (Pakatan Harapan-Bukit Gelugor) and Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (Barisan Nasional-Simpang Renggam) as the government’s representatives, with Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (Perikatan Nasional-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) representing the Opposition.
The two senators are similarly nominated by the Dewan Negara’s Committee of Selection and approved by a resolution of the Senate.
Dewan Negara president Datuk Seri Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah has said the two senators will be appointed once the Dewan Negara convenes from November 30.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul has said the council is expected to be formed by December.
The council also includes the clerk to the Dewan Negara and the clerk to the Dewan Rakyat.
Its three ex-officio members are the Treasury secretary-general or a representative, the director-general of Public Service or a representative, and Parliament’s chief administrator.
Ex-officio members do not have voting rights.
That leaves 13 voting members, of whom two are Opposition MPs.
This composition brings together parliamentary leaders, government and Opposition representatives, and officials from the Treasury, the Public Service Department and Parliament’s administration.
What does the council actually do?
The Act gives the council four broad responsibilities.
First, it appoints members of the Parliamentary Service and determines their terms and conditions of appointment, subject to the applicable legal framework.
Second, it oversees financial matters relating to the service.
Third, it develops and implements training and development programmes for Parliamentary Service staff.
Fourth, it may take other steps reasonably necessary to administer the service and carry out its functions.
These responsibilities matter because Parliament needs professional staff to support its proceedings, maintain official records, assist committees and handle legislative and administrative work.
The council may also establish committees to help carry out its responsibilities.
Does the council run Parliament day to day?
Not directly, as the Act hands that job to Parliament’s chief administrator.
The chief administrator is responsible for the institution’s overall administration and management, including its day-to-day affairs and the financial matters of the Parliamentary Service.
The chief administrator acts under the council’s general authority and directions, and is also the council’s secretary.
This creates a division of responsibility: the council oversees the service and provides general direction, while the chief administrator handles its administration and daily operations.
The Act also provides for separate committees dealing with staff promotions, disciplinary matters and appeals.
How will the council make decisions?
The council must meet as often as necessary to carry out its functions.
At least seven members are required for a quorum.
Members other than ex-officio members are entitled to vote, and decisions are made by a majority of those present and voting.
If the votes are tied, the chairman has a casting vote.
The Act also requires members to disclose any direct or indirect interest in a matter being considered.
A member with such an interest cannot take part in the relevant deliberations or decision.
These provisions establish formal procedures for decision-making and help guard against conflicts of interest.
How will it make Parliament more independent?
The central idea is to give Parliament greater control over its own administrative needs, rather than relying on arrangements managed through the executive branch.
When the Parliamentary Service Bill was before Parliament in 2025, Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the service was intended to strengthen Parliament’s institutional independence and support the separation of powers between the legislative, executive and judicial branches.
She also highlighted the need for professional support for MPs, including help with drafting legislation and access to research expertise for both government and Opposition lawmakers.
Such support could help MPs and parliamentary committees examine bills, assess government policies and scrutinise public spending more effectively.
However, the council itself does not hold the government politically accountable.
Its role is to manage the administrative support that Parliament needs to perform its oversight functions, while MPs and parliamentary committees remain responsible for carrying out that scrutiny.
Will Parliament control its own budget?
Not entirely, because the Act leaves it to the government to provide the funds.
Section 12 of the Act provides that the government must supply sufficient funds annually for the Parliamentary Service to enable the council to perform its functions.
The council is responsible for overseeing financial matters relating to the service, but the statutory provision does not itself spell out every step in the budget-submission process.
Azalina said that the intended arrangement would allow Parliament to submit budget proposals directly to the Finance Ministry without first obtaining approval from the Prime Minister’s Department.
That distinction matters: the obligation to provide sufficient funding is set out in the law, while the direct-submission procedure is part of the minister’s explanation of how the arrangement is intended to work.
Does this mean Parliament is completely separate from the civil service?
No, as the Act keeps links between the Parliamentary Service and the wider public administration.
The Act establishes the Parliamentary Service as a service separate from the general public service.
For example, Section 11 requires the Chief Administrator to be appointed from among members of the federal general public service.
The arrangement therefore gives Parliament a distinct administrative structure under the law without severing all connections with the wider public service and government financial systems.
What does this mean for accountability?
The council creates a formal structure for managing Parliament’s staff, finances and administrative resources, with rules governing appointments, training, voting and conflicts of interest.
Azalina has argued that stronger institutional support would help MPs serve as the “eyes and ears of the people”, including by enabling them to identify wastage and hold the government accountable.
But a new administrative structure alone cannot guarantee more effective scrutiny.
That will also depend on whether MPs make effective use of the support available to them, how parliamentary committees conduct their work and how well the council fulfils its responsibilities.
Ultimately, the council’s significance lies in helping Parliament manage the resources it needs to do its job, while leaving the responsibility for questioning the government and holding it accountable with MPs and parliamentary committees.

Title: Faced with an ageing fleet, Malaysia's fire department turns to robots and upgrades
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) is strengthening its operational and logistical capabilities through asset modernisation efforts and the exploration of new technologies, including Unmanned Remote Systems (URS) involving two Fire Fighting Robots (FFRs).
JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the move was crucial for ensuring the department remained prepared to deal with various emergencies, including fires, accidents, rescue operations and large-scale disasters.
He said the replacement of vehicles and equipment would be carried out in stages based on the age and operational capability of existing assets, including the acquisition of 80 Fire Rescue Tenders (FRTs).
According to him, JBPM acquired 686 FRT units between 2001 and 2026, while the requirement based on operational norm stood at 592 units.
“Based on these figures, 372 of the 592 existing units (63 per cent) have exceeded 10 years of service. As such, the procurement of 80 replacement FRT units and 150 existing CFRT (Compact Fire Rescue Tender) units is expected to have a tangible impact on the department’s preparedness and operational capabilities and service delivery in the coming years,” he told Bernama.
Besides replacing vehicles, Nor Hisham said the department was also focusing on improving response times, especially in areas that had yet to meet the stipulated targets, through the construction of new fire stations and the continuation of ongoing projects.
Rescue personnel participate in a disaster response exercise as part of preparations for the North-east Monsoon season. — Bernama pic
“In a bid to modernise our operational capabilities, the department also plans to acquire URS equipment involving two FFR units, in line with technological advancements to support firefighting and rescue operations.
“The provision of personal protective equipment (PPE), particularly firefighting protective clothing, as well as the addition and replacement of basic rescue equipment, are also important requirements to ensure the safety of personnel while on duty,” he added.
Nor Hisham said the department was also focusing on utility vehicles, logistics for its K9 Unit and operational facilities to support personnel mobility, especially during search and rescue operations and disaster management.
In terms of personnel welfare, the JBPM is focusing on the construction and maintenance of quarters, with total project costs amounting to RM241.6 million, including a ceiling allocation of RM35.1 million for 2027.
A total of RM16 million has also been allocated for facility maintenance, in addition to the approval of redevelopment and modernisation of ageing fire stations, namely the Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) in Perai, Jalan Perak, Jerantut, Muar and Sarikei.
Nor Hisham expects efforts to strengthen assets, facilities and personnel capabilities to improve asset reliability, departmental preparedness and emergency response capabilities.
In the long term, JBPM is open to exploring the use of electric vehicles (EVs) for FRTs and utility vehicles, with assessments to be conducted on operational suitability, travel distances, battery capacity, charging infrastructure, technical requirements and the total lifecycle cost of the assets.
To support these efforts, the government has approved a Development Expenditure (DE) allocation of RM1.8 billion for JBPM under Budget 2027 to carry out 96 ongoing and new projects, comprising physical development, infrastructure and the procurement of vehicles and equipment, with a ceiling allocation of RM200 million for the year.
A Fire and Rescue Department helicopter is deployed during a search and rescue operation in Bidor, Perak. — Bernama pic
“This allocation is extremely important, particularly in meeting the need to replace FRTs, provide protective clothing and other firefighting and rescue equipment,” he added.
On Saturday (Oct 24), Minister of Housing and Local Government Nga Kor Ming announced the allocation of RM200 million under Budget 2027 to enhance firefighters’ efficiency in carrying out rescue missions and preparedness for fire-related disasters. — Bernama

Title: China still tops list of international students in Malaysia, but other markets are growing, says EMGS
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — While China remains Malaysia’s largest source of international students, the Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) said applications from other countries are growing.
EMGS chairman Datuk Ahmad Shalimin Ahmad Shaffie said China accounted for approximately 41 per cent of applications in 2023, but the proportion has since declined as Malaysia attracts students from more markets.
“By 2025, East Asia as a whole, including China, accounted for less than 37 per cent. In the first four months of 2026, China’s share stood at approximately 27 per cent.
“Alongside continued growth in total applications, these figures indicate an increasingly important contribution from other markets,” he said in a statement.
Ahmad Shalimin said regional figures further reflected this growing diversity.
“In 2025, applications from South Asia and Central Asia each grew by 41 per cent, while South-east Asia recorded 28 per cent growth, Africa by 20 per cent and the Middle East and North Africa by 19 per cent.
“Over the past decade, EMGS has received applications from 189 countries,” he added.
He said this was why the question raised by Gareth Liu Zi Yuan in his article, “More international students, but from where?”, published in Malay Mail on October 22, deserved attention.
“We welcome the discussion on broadening Malaysia’s international student community and ensuring that those who come here receive a rewarding education and experience.
“Malaysia is ranked 14th globally as an international education destination, welcoming students from nearly 180 countries. That reach provides a strong foundation,” he said.
However, Ahmad Shalimin said Malaysia must now strengthen existing connections, develop opportunities in underrepresented markets and ensure international students have good reasons to recommend the country after graduation.
He said EMGS conducts marketing activities across seven regions, with more than 50 programmes worldwide each year.
“Education fairs, forums, international exhibitions, school visits and counsellor engagements connect Malaysian institutions with students, families and education partners across different markets.
“Recent efforts have included Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Kenya, Türkiye and Central Asia, alongside participation in the European Association for International Education exhibition in Glasgow,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said engagement with neighbouring ASEAN countries, particularly Indonesia, and nearby regions such as South Asia remained a priority.
“These efforts also include creating more accessible pathways for students through mobility programmes and scholarship opportunities.
“By strengthening established partnerships while developing opportunities in emerging markets, Malaysia can broaden its international student community and build lasting education connections,” he said.
He added that student mobility programmes were also strengthening Malaysia’s ties with Europe.
“The number of mobility students from France increased from 827 in 2025 to 939 in 2026, a rise of 13.5 per cent, reflecting continued interest in Malaysia for short-term international study experiences,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said Malaysia’s international education presence was also expanding through local universities operating overseas.
“UCSI University’s campus in Dhaka, established in 2023, became Bangladesh’s first approved foreign university branch campus.
“It brings Malaysian education closer to students in their home country while strengthening the international presence of our institutions,” he said.
He said these developments reflected the growing international recognition of Malaysia’s higher education sector.
“Universiti Malaya is ranked 56th in the QS World University Rankings 2027 and joint 194th in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027.
“Sunway University’s position as 11th globally for International Outlook in the latter rankings further illustrates the international engagement of Malaysia’s public and private institutions,” he said.
“For prospective students, these achievements help make Malaysia’s educational strengths visible. For our institutions, they reinforce the importance of sustained academic quality and international cooperation,” he added.
On student pass applications, Ahmad Shalimin said EMGS facilitates digital submissions, document verification, academic screening and application tracking, while the Immigration Department of Malaysia remains the approving authority.
“EMGS’s published processing charter is 14 working days for complete applications. Alya, our AI-powered assistant, also answers queries around the clock, helping students navigate visa requirements and application procedures.
“Upon arrival, the International Student Arrival Centres (ISAC) at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2 provide round-the-clock assistance before immigration clearance, including guidance on access to dedicated lanes.
“This dedicated support helps students navigate their first experience in Malaysia with greater confidence,” he said.
He also said EMGS offered internship opportunities to international students, having welcomed interns from Iran, Myanmar, Indonesia, Turkmenistan and several African countries.
“These placements provide opportunities to apply knowledge, develop professional skills and experience a Malaysian workplace.
“Support from higher education institutions is equally vital through career guidance, industry partnerships and internship opportunities that prepare students for their future careers,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said internationalisation also benefited Malaysian students studying alongside their international counterparts.
“Shared classrooms, research and community activities expose students to different perspectives and help them build international networks within their own campuses.
“As Malaysian universities become better known abroad, employers and academic partners become more familiar with their qualifications and expertise.
“The relationships developed through education can support future research, institutional cooperation and professional opportunities,” he said.
He added that international graduates also helped strengthen Malaysia’s global connections.
“Their experiences influence what families, colleagues and future students understand about Malaysia. They become informal ambassadors whose achievements and personal stories give our higher education sector a human face,” he said.
Ahmad Shalimin said studying in Malaysia should offer international students more than just an academic qualification.
“Learning alongside people from different backgrounds, participating in community life and navigating new experiences can nurture empathy, resilience and a stronger sense of responsibility.
“Our ambition is for students to leave with the knowledge to pursue their careers and the character to contribute meaningfully to society, carrying a lasting connection with Malaysia wherever life takes them,” he said.

Title: First the floods, then the heat: MetMalaysia warns of challenging months ahead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Malaysia may experience hotter and drier weather towards the end of the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon (MTL), especially from late January to March next year, following expectations of a Super El Niño phenomenon that could lead to reduced rainfall across the country
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said these conditions could increase the risk of heatwaves and droughts, especially if rainfall decreases during that period.
He said the El Niño phenomenon is currently in a strong phase and is expected to intensify to a very strong level or Super El Niño towards the end of this year and into next year.
“With reduced rainfall, hot weather or heatwaves often emerge, along with drought due to water shortages caused by insufficient rainfall,” he said as a guest on Bernama TV’s “Fokus 15” programme today.
However, he said the initial phase of the 2026/2027 MTL, which begins today, is expected to bring three to five episodes of prolonged heavy rainfall, particularly between this November and January 2027.
He said that these conditions could heighten the risk of flooding, particularly in the East Coast states of Kelantan, Terengganu and Pahang, as well as eastern Johor.
“Residents in flood-prone areas should remain vigilant regarding the risk of heavy rain during the early part of the monsoon, while drier conditions towards the end of the monsoon will require preparations for possible hot weather and water shortages,” he said.
Maqrun Fadzli said MetMalaysia monitors weather developments around the clock and will issue heavy rain warnings when necessary to enable relevant agencies and the public to take appropriate precautionary measures.
He advised the public to always refer to latest weather information and warnings from official sources, make early preparations for possible floods and comply with instructions from the authorities, including evacuation orders when necessary.
He also reminded the public to avoid open burning during the dry weather to reduce the risk of localised haze. — Bernama

Title: Maritime officer killed, three injured during pursuit of suspected migrant boat off Perlis
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 27 — A Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) personnel was killed and three others injured when their boat collided with a concrete structure during an enforcement operation off Kuala Sungai Padang, Kuala Perlis, last night.
Kedah and Perlis Maritime director First Admiral Romli Mustafa said five MMEA personnel were conducting the operation at 11.37pm to intercept a boat suspected of carrying undocumented Myanmar migrants.
He said the suspected migrant boat sped towards the shore after being detected, triggering a 15-minute pursuit. The boat is believed to have rammed the MMEA vessel, causing it to collide with a concrete structure near the Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM) jetty at Kuala Sungai Padang.
“The impact threw three of the five personnel overboard, including one who was reported missing. He was found floating in the sea at about 1.30am today, unconscious, and was pronounced dead. He was believed to have sustained serious head injuries,” he told a press conference here today.
Romli said the three injured personnel suffered a fractured wrist, chest pain, and pain on both sides of the ribs. All were taken to Hospital Tuanku Fauziah for further examination and treatment.
The deceased was taken to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital in Alor Setar, Kedah, for a post-mortem. His remains are expected to be buried in his hometown at Kuala Nerang, Kedah, after Asar prayers.
The deceased was identified as Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan, 41, an MMEA technical personnel.
Romli said nine suspected undocumented Myanmar migrants, comprising seven men and two women, and two Thai male boat operators were detained in the incident.
“Checks found that all those detained were suspected of offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM).
“They have been taken to the Kuala Perlis Maritime Zone headquarters for further investigation,” he said.
Romli said the MMEA would investigate the incident to determine its exact cause, stressing that personnel safety remained a priority during enforcement operations.
He added that efforts to combat the entry of undocumented migrants through the country’s maritime routes would continue to be strengthened.
The MMEA also extended its condolences to the deceased’s family and expressed appreciation for his service in protecting the country’s waters. — Bernama

Title: More than 10,000 visitors expected at National Deepavali celebration in Brickfields on Nov 14
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — More than 10,000 visitors are expected at the National Deepavali Celebration organised by the National Unity Ministry (KPN) in Brickfields here on November 14.
Deputy Minister R. Yuneswaran said the event, expected to be officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, would feature arts, culture and heritage activities from morning until night, including performances by artistes and unique exhibitions such as Rumah Malaysia.
“We are targeting more than 10,000 visitors on the day, as it falls on a Saturday. We hope many people will attend,” he told reporters at a hi-tea session with the media here today.
Yuneswaran called on media practitioners to work with the ministry and relevant departments to promote unity and social harmony, urging them to move away from issues related to the 3Rs (race, religion and royalty) or anything that could undermine social harmony.
“We can see significant changes in the unity index across the states. People out there are actually more united,” he said. — Bernama
